rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract CLIN schedule and the contract performance report be obtained to establish what CLIN 0001 covers and to reconcile the CLIN-level completion measure with the whole-contract work-completed measure?
rows.target_document: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) contracting file / NAVSEA 02 contracts office
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-79 and CVN-80 contract notes and footnotes from the most recent CVN 78 class Selected Acquisition Report / MSAR contract-status tables, and compare the CVN-79 note's completion-measure wording with the CVN-80 note's CLIN 0001-dollars wording; a single read of the two notes side by side either shows the measurement basis is already stated or shows it is not. No contracting-file access needed.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class SAR/MSAR contract-status table notes for CVN-79 and CVN-80 DD&C
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE / Navy SAR reporting office
rows.period: most recent SAR/MSAR reporting year
rows.account: CVN 78 class acquisition (carrier replacement procurement line 2001)
rows.hypothesis: The gap is not a document-access problem at all for the CLIN-definition half: CLIN 0001 scope is already defined in the open SAR/MSAR contract notes and the CVN-80 DD&C note (which measures completion in CLIN 0001 dollars) supplies the convention by analogy, meaning the only truly missing item is the CLIN schedule's exact work statement, not the completion-measurement basis.

rows.instruction: Request from PMS 378 only the CLIN-level obligation/expenditure summary (not the full contract) for the CVN-79 DD&C contract, showing CLIN 0001 value against total contract value for the reporting period, and confirm whether the reported completion percentage's denominator is CLIN 0001 or the contract total.
rows.target_system: Navy ERP / contract CLIN financial summary
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) business financial manager
rows.period: current and prior reporting year
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract, CLIN 0001 vs total contract
rows.hypothesis: The two measures cannot be reconciled because they are not the same kind of measure: the whole-contract work-completed figure is a dollar-weighted measure, so the apparent CLIN-vs-contract discrepancy is a denominator difference (CLIN 0001 dollars vs total contract dollars) rather than a disagreement about physical progress, and no hull-level physical progress can be derived from either.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification (the one moving planned post-shakedown work into construction and adjusting delivery) from the PMS 378 contracting file modification log, and read only the CLIN-affected block to see which CLIN absorbed the moved work and whether CLIN 0001's statement of work changed. Source of the label: the question text and the SAR contract note, neither of which is the contract.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract modification log and the June 2023 modification SF-30 / CLIN schedule pages
rows.target_system: Electronic Document Access (EDA) / Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 02 contracts office
rows.period: June 2023 through present
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract modification, June 2023
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label in the question -- that CLIN 0001 is the detail design and construction scope whose completion equals hull construction progress -- is wrong or incomplete; CLIN 0001 may exclude or include scope moved by contract modification, so the label arrived with the question rather than from the contract.

rows.instruction: Check the CSDR compliance status entry for the CVN 78 class program in the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise (CADE) submission tracking record for the reporting period, and confirm whether CVN-79 DD&C contractor cost data reports were accepted, rejected or waived; a rejected or missing submission kills the retrieval path immediately.
rows.target_system: CADE (Cost Assessment Data Enterprise) CSDR compliance record
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE Defense Cost and Resource Center
rows.period: reporting period of the Red rating through present
rows.account: CVN 78 class / CVN-79 DD&C CSDR submissions
rows.hypothesis: The reconciliation is blocked by a reporting-data defect rather than document access: the program's Cost and Software Data Reporting compliance is rated Red, so the contract performance report's CLIN-level cost/work data may be non-compliant or absent for the period in question, and an anticipated future Green rating does not make the data currently usable.

rows.instruction: Obtain the CVN-79 Integrated Program Management Report (CPR/IPMR) Format 1 and Format 5 for the months immediately before and after the delivery-strategy revision from the PMS 378 EVM analyst's file, and compare the budget-at-completion lines by CLIN/WBS across the re-baseline point.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 IPMR Formats 1 and 5
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) EVM / cost analysis cell
rows.period: three months before and after the delivery-strategy change
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C performance measurement baseline
rows.hypothesis: A contract performance report exists but its baseline was re-set by the delivery-strategy change, so the CLIN-level completion measure in the current report is not on the same baseline as the whole-contract measure cited in the question, making reconciliation impossible without the pre- and post-revision baselines.

rows.instruction: Compare the CVN-79 DD&C CLIN titles against the CVN 78 subprogram funding-source table in the PB 2025 SAR supplement, confirming whether outfitting and construction-preparation scope sit on separate procurement lines outside the DD&C CLIN structure and whether the PB 2025 class estimate uses a four-carrier quantity; one table read disconfirms the hull-level mapping.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class SAR supplement funding-source table
rows.target_office: PMS 378 program financial management
rows.account: CVN 78 subprogram funding-source table; carrier-replacement line 2001 and outfitting line
rows.hypothesis: Even if both documents are obtained, they will not support a hull-level progress and cost basis, because the CLIN structure and the reported class estimates are organized by class and by separate procurement lines (construction-preparation, outfitting, carrier-replacement line 2001) rather than by hull, so the blocked conversion fails on structure rather than on access.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the cited source estimating references for the antecedent carrier operating and support estimate, specifically the June 2022 OPNAV 4700 letter, the CVN 68 Ship Manpower Document, and the underlying VAMOSC extract, be obtained to reproduce the antecedent O&S comparison?
rows.target_document: OPNAV N9 / NAVSEA cost engineering (VAMOSC program office)
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the OPNAV N9 official correspondence/record tracking registry for OPNAV 4700-series letters signed in June 2022 concerning carrier depot maintenance requirements; request the control number, signature authority and distribution/classification marking only. If no 4700-series letter of that month appears in the registry, the cited reference is mislabeled and the request stops here.
rows.target_document: June 2022 OPNAV 4700 letter
rows.target_office: OPNAV N9 correspondence/records registry
rows.period: June 2022
rows.account: CVN 78 class antecedent (CVN 68) O&S estimate — depot maintenance element
rows.hypothesis: The three cited sources are not a single retrievable package but internal estimating references held only inside the antecedent O&S estimate's documentation file; the June 2022 OPNAV 4700 letter exists as a signed OPNAV correspondence item retrievable from the OPNAV N9 correspondence/tasker registry, and its retrievability can be settled by a single registry lookup before any attempt to obtain the other two.

rows.instruction: Pull the source-citation footnotes and reference list of the 2023 program-office O&S estimate documentation that the MSAR O&S comparison draws its current estimate from, and compare the verbatim citation string for the depot-maintenance source against the gap's label; identify which document first asserted the 'OPNAV 4700' attribution.
rows.target_document: 2023 POE O&S documentation reference list and MSAR O&S section footnotes
rows.target_office: OPNAV N9 / NAVSEA cost engineering
rows.period: 2023 program-office O&S estimate of record
rows.account: Antecedent O&S depot maintenance element — source citation
rows.hypothesis: The label 'June 2022 OPNAV 4700 letter' is an inherited citation carried forward from the MSAR/program-office O&S write-up and may misstate the series, date or originating office (e.g. a 4700-series maintenance requirements message versus an N9 letter), making the document unobtainable as cited rather than genuinely withheld.

rows.instruction: Request from OPNAV N1 / NAVMAC the CVN 68 Ship Manpower Document version in force for the antecedent estimate, and separately request the authorized-billet (activity manpower document) extract used for the manpower element, for the estimate's base year; confirm whether the billet file alone reproduces the manpower component.
rows.target_document: CVN 68 Ship Manpower Document and authorized billet extract
rows.target_office: NAVMAC / OPNAV N1
rows.period: antecedent estimate base year
rows.account: Antecedent O&S manpower element — authorized billets / OSD composite rates
rows.hypothesis: The CVN 68 Ship Manpower Document is obtainable but through a manpower authority rather than the cost community, because the antecedent manpower element was built from authorized billets rather than from the SMD itself; the SMD may therefore be a corroborating rather than a driving reference, and a billet-file substitute may already satisfy reproduction.

rows.instruction: Ask the NAVSEA VAMOSC program office for the query audit log / saved-report definition behind the antecedent CVN 68 extract: ship set, fiscal years, forward-deployed exclusion flag, cost elements selected, and extract date; request the archived data vintage corresponding to that pull date rather than a current pull.
rows.target_office: NAVSEA cost engineering (VAMOSC program office)
rows.period: full fiscal years used in the antecedent estimate
rows.account: CVN 68 antecedent O&S — VAMOSC-sourced elements
rows.hypothesis: The VAMOSC extract is obtainable only as a parameterized re-query, not as an archived file, because the antecedent used full-year VAMOSC data with forward-deployed ships excluded; without the original filter set, date of pull and data-vintage, the extract cannot be reproduced even with system access granted.

rows.instruction: Request from the NAVSEA cost engineering originating office the distribution statement, classification and proprietary markings for each of the three references, plus any existing denial or FOIA-exemption determination; do not request content.
rows.target_office: NAVSEA cost engineering / originating document custodians
rows.period: current
rows.account: Antecedent O&S estimate source package — releasability
rows.hypothesis: Access is the binding constraint rather than existence: the three references are classified, CUI, or contractor-proprietary at a level that bars release to the requester, and the closability finding of 'access_required' reflects a releasability determination that can be read off the documents' own markings without obtaining their content.

rows.instruction: Obtain from OPNAV N9 / CAPE the cost-element-structure crosswalk mapping the 2015 independent-cost-estimate O&S categories to the structure used in the 2023 program-office estimate, specifically the disposition of indirect support element 6.0, for the CVN 78 class O&S comparison.
rows.target_document: CAPE O&S cost element structure crosswalk
rows.target_office: OPNAV N9 / OSD CAPE
rows.period: 2015 ICE versus 2023 POE
rows.account: O&S comparison cost element structure — element 6.0 and antecedent categories
rows.hypothesis: Even if all three references are obtained, the antecedent O&S comparison cannot be reproduced from them, because the comparison's structure changed after the 2015 estimate (indirect-support element 6.0 omitted under the revised CAPE cost structure); the missing retrievable is the CAPE cost-element-structure crosswalk, not the three cited sources.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can SECNAV M-5200.45 and the cited DON financial-reporting references, including reference (w) and enclosure (2) paragraph 4l asset-list specifications, be obtained to establish the prescribed equipment valuation, CIP relief, and quarterly reporting record formats and whether those records identify CVN-79?
rows.target_document: ASN (FM&C) Office of Financial Operations
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the Department of the Navy Issuances website / SECNAV directives control point (DON/AA Directives and Records Management Division) master index for the 5200-series and 7000-series manuals current and cancelled, for the issuance effective period covering CVN-79 construction, and pull the enclosure (2) table of contents plus the reference list to confirm whether a reference (w) and a paragraph 4l asset-list specification exist in that manual at all.
rows.target_document: SECNAV M-5200.45 (asserted designator) and SECNAV directives master index
rows.target_office: DON/AA Directives and Records Management Division
rows.period: issuance in force during CVN-79 construction period
rows.account: N/A - document control
rows.hypothesis: The inherited document label is wrong: "SECNAV M-5200.45" as cited in the question (and its internal reference (w) / enclosure (2) paragraph 4l) may be a mis-transcribed or superseded designator for the DON general-equipment / accountable-property financial-reporting manual actually in force, meaning the prescribed valuation, CIP-relief and quarterly-reporting formats exist but under a different control number. The label arrived with the question, not from a verified citation.

rows.instruction: Attempt direct retrieval from the DON Issuances public library and the FMO/ASN (FM&C) Financial Management Policy Manual library; if CAC-gated, request the distribution-statement page only from the ASN (FM&C) Office of Financial Operations action officer named as executor, citing the issuance number and enclosure (2).
rows.target_document: SECNAV M-5200.45 distribution statement and enclosure (2)
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) Office of Financial Operations
rows.period: current edition plus prior editions
rows.account: N/A - document access
rows.hypothesis: The manual is unclassified and publicly posted, and the access barrier is procedural (portal/CAC-gated hosting) rather than a withholding determination, so the prescribed formats are obtainable without a records request.

rows.instruction: Read enclosure (2) paragraph 4l data-element list and the asset roll-forward template field list; compare against the UII and local-tag field definitions to determine whether any prescribed field carries a ship hull designator. Request the template from ASN (FM&C) Office of Financial Operations for the quarterly submissions covering CVN-79 construction years.
rows.target_document: SECNAV M-5200.45 enclosure (2) para 4l asset-list data-element specification and quarterly roll-forward template
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) Office of Financial Operations
rows.period: quarterly submissions, CVN-79 construction years
rows.account: General equipment / CIP general-ledger accounts
rows.hypothesis: Even if the manual is obtained, its prescribed quarterly asset-list format may be specified only at the account/general-ledger summary level and not require a hull or end-item identifier, so no prescribed record format would carry CVN-79-identifiable equipment valuation; the hull linkage would have to come from the APSR data fields instead.

rows.instruction: Identify the funding BSO for CVN-79 general-equipment procurement (NAVSEA / PEO Aircraft Carriers supporting BSO) and request from its Command Property Officer the quarterly asset lists and roll-forward submissions as transmitted to ASN (FM&C), for the construction-period quarters; cross-check ASN (FM&C) receipt logs for the same quarters.
rows.target_document: BSO quarterly asset list and asset roll-forward submissions to ASN (FM&C)
rows.target_office: NAVSEA / PEO Aircraft Carriers supporting BSO Command Property Officer
rows.period: CVN-79 construction-period quarters
rows.account: General equipment, construction-in-progress
rows.hypothesis: The responsive records sit with the funding BSO rather than with ASN (FM&C), because the BSO that funded the CVN-79 general-equipment procurement retains financial-reporting responsibility until formal transfer; the executor named in the question may hold only the aggregated receipt, not the hull-level asset list.

rows.instruction: Obtain from ASN (FM&C), coordinating with the DON Office of the Chief Management Officer, the approved-APSR list in force for Navy general equipment during the CVN-79 construction period; then request from the designated APSR the CIP project records and relief transactions coded to the CVN-79 construction project, with the cost/receipt/transfer document agreement evidence.
rows.target_document: ASN (FM&C) approved-APSR list; APSR CIP project and relief transaction extract
rows.target_system: Navy-directed Accountable Property System of Record
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) / DON Office of the Chief Management Officer
rows.period: CVN-79 construction through CIP completion
rows.account: Construction-in-progress project account for CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The hull-identifiable evidence exists in the approved APSR and its CIP-relief transaction trail rather than in the manual's reporting formats, so the manual only points to the system of record; the gap is closable through APSR extracts showing project-cost relief at CIP completion.

rows.instruction: Pull the PIEE GFP module property records and GFP attachments for the CVN-79 construction contract from the administering contracting office (SUPSHIP Newport News / NAVSEA PEO Carriers contracting), for the construction period, and compare the GFP/CAP transfer documentation against the designated APSR accountable records to determine whether DON accountable records were ever established.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract GFP attachments and PIEE GFP module property transfer records
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News / NAVSEA contracting office
rows.period: CVN-79 construction contract period of performance
rows.account: Government-furnished and contractor-acquired property on the CVN-79 contract
rows.hypothesis: No DON-held prescribed record carries the hull-level equipment valuation because the property was contractor-acquired and tracked in the shipbuilder's property system; the government APSR record may be thin or absent, which the manual forbids but which would explain the retrieval failure rather than a document-access problem.

rows.instruction: query: Can the responsible Budget Submitting Office provide its quarterly asset-universe submissions for the CVN-79 asset balances, including the APSR-to-general-ledger reconciliations, the budgetary-reporting reconciliation, field-level journal vouchers, and trial-balance extraction parameters?
rows.target_system: NAVSEA Budget Submitting Office financial reporting / ASN (FM&C) quarterly submission repository
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from ASN (FM&C) financial reporting the BSO-assignment/crosswalk listing which BSO code carries financial-reporting responsibility for the CVN-79 (PEO Carriers / PMS 379) general-equipment and CIP accounts for the quarters at issue, plus any written allocation-of-reporting-responsibility memorandum or formal transfer documentation stating whether ownership and financial reporting, or only custody, moved.
rows.target_document: BSO reporting-responsibility assignment and transfer documentation
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) financial reporting / NAVSEA Comptroller BSO coordination
rows.period: Each quarter-end and year-end in the period under review
rows.account: General equipment and construction-in-progress (CIP) for CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label naming NAVSEA's BSO as the responsible submitter is wrong: CVN-79 hull equipment and CIP balances may report through a different funding BSO (or through PEO Aircraft Carriers' supporting BSO), so the request was addressed to an office that never held the submission. This attribution arrived with the question's NAMED EXECUTOR line and has not been tested.

rows.instruction: Ask ASN (FM&C) to produce the receipt log / submission index of the quarterly asset-universe reporting repository, filtered to the responsible BSO code and to CVN-79 general-equipment and CIP accounts, for each quarter in scope; then pull the same quarters' entries from the specified reporting system or its Data Collection Module transaction/summary upload history.
rows.target_system: Designated general-equipment reporting system and its Data Collection Module
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) quarterly submission repository
rows.period: All in-scope quarters
rows.account: Quarterly asset-universe submission package (equipment and CIP)
rows.hypothesis: The submissions exist and were received, but only in the ASN (FM&C) quarterly repository or the designated reporting system's Data Collection Module, not in the BSO's own files -- so the gap is a retrieval-location error rather than a records-nonexistence or access problem.

rows.instruction: For a single named quarter, request from the responsible BSO's financial-reporting branch the component-level inventory of that quarter's asset-universe package -- specifically the APSR-to-general-ledger reconciliation worksheet, the budgetary-entry-to-asset-list reconciliation, the field-level journal voucher file, and the documented trial-balance extraction parameters (query/report definitions) -- and record which components have no corresponding file.
rows.target_document: Quarterly asset-universe submission component inventory
rows.target_office: Responsible BSO financial reporting branch
rows.period: One pilot quarter, then expand
rows.account: CVN-79 asset balances within the quarterly asset-universe package
rows.hypothesis: The submissions were made but are incomplete as to the four named components: the APSR-to-GL reconciliation, the budgetary-reporting-to-asset-list reconciliation, field-level journal vouchers, and trial-balance extraction parameters are separable deliverables, and one or more (most likely the extraction parameters and the JVs) were never included, which is why the package cannot be produced as asked.

rows.instruction: Obtain the current ASN (FM&C)-approved APSR list and the CNO determination of which approved APSRs the Navy may use, then ask the BSO Command Property Officer which designated APSR holds the CVN-79 hull-equipment and GFP records; compare against any contractor property system of record cited in the shipbuilding contract's property clauses.
rows.target_document: APSR approval list and CPO system recommendation package
rows.target_system: Approved APSR list vs. contractor property system
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) APSR approval authority; BSO Command Property Officer
rows.period: Current and the in-scope quarters
rows.account: Accountable general equipment and GFP associated with CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: CVN-79 balances are not in an approved APSR in the form the request assumes: the equipment may be tracked only in the shipbuilder's contractor property system, or in a system not on the ASN (FM&C) approved-APSR list, so no APSR-derived asset list exists to reconcile to the general ledger.

rows.instruction: Request from PEO Aircraft Carriers / the CVN-79 program office the quarterly CIP project-cost review records and the annual CIP-accrual-to-contract-progress reconciliation for the in-scope years, plus APSR evidence that cost, receipt, and transfer documents agree and that relieved or expensed project costs were posted on project completion or cancellation.
rows.target_document: Quarterly CIP review and annual CIP accrual reconciliation files
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers program office (PM / requiring official) with BSO financial reporting
rows.period: Each quarter plus annual reconciliation in the in-scope years
rows.account: CVN-79 construction-in-progress account
rows.hypothesis: The CIP side of the gap reflects missing periodic CIP review and relief documentation rather than a missing quarterly submission: if quarterly CIP cost reviews and the annual accrual-to-contract-progress reconciliation were not performed or not documented, the CIP balances have no traceable support to offer, and completed/cancelled project relief entries may be unrecorded in the APSR.

rows.instruction: Submit a single written access request to ASN (FM&C) financial reporting naming the quarters, the BSO code, and the four artifact types, and ask in the same letter who the release authority is for each artifact and which office holds the APO auditable transaction trail; a refusal letter identifying the authority kills or confirms this hypothesis in one exchange.
rows.target_document: Access/release determination correspondence
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) financial reporting release authority and the accountable property officer of record
rows.period: All in-scope quarters
rows.account: All four requested artifact types for CVN-79 asset balances
rows.hypothesis: The stated blocker is genuinely access/authorization rather than existence: the submissions and reconciliations are held but release is withheld pending data-sensitivity, system-account, or separation-of-duties constraints, including the rule that property-accountability and financial-accounting roles for the same property be held separately, which can split custody of the requested artifacts across two offices that each lack full release authority.

rows.instruction: ask, and record the answer before it retires: Which lifecycle-management responsibilities for CVN-79 equipment are assigned under the cited DON lifecycle-management reference, and which PEO and supporting BSO therefore carry financial accountability and reporting for that equipment?
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) with NAVSEA Command Property Officer
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the cited DON lifecycle-management reference (the SECNAV/ASN (FM&C) general-equipment accountability instruction named in the gap's citation field) and read only the responsibilities enclosure and the definitions section; confirm or refute by name whether PMS 378 and the NAVSEA Command Property Officer appear as the assigned lifecycle-management and property-accountability roles for carrier hull equipment. Record which source in the dossier first asserted the PMS 378 / NAVSEA CPO pairing (SME interview note vs. budget exhibit) and whether that source cited the instruction or inferred it.
rows.target_document: Cited DON lifecycle-management reference (SECNAVINST/ASN (FM&C) general-equipment accountability instruction), responsibilities and definitions sections
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) Financial Reporting / Office of Financial Operations
rows.period: Instruction version in force for the gap's reporting period
rows.account: CVN-79 hull equipment, general equipment accountability
rows.hypothesis: The inherited attribution in the gap record — that PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) with the NAVSEA Command Property Officer is the office carrying lifecycle-management responsibility and financial accountability for CVN-79 equipment — is a label that arrived with the question and was never checked against the cited DON lifecycle-management reference. The reference may assign lifecycle responsibility to the program manager designation by hull/program rather than to PMS 378 as stated, and the Command Property Officer role in the reference is a recommender of APSRs through the BSO chain, not an accountability holder.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the BSO code and funding line on the CVN-79 equipment procurement documents for the gap period and compare against the BSO roster submitting quarterly general-equipment financial reports to ASN (FM&C); request from NAVSEA FMB the BSO designation under which PMS 378 reports. Kill the hypothesis if the funding BSO and the PEO's supporting BSO are the same code.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 equipment procurement funding documents and BSO quarterly general-equipment financial submission
rows.target_system: BSO quarterly reporting system or its Data Collection Module
rows.target_office: NAVSEA FMB / ASN (FM&C) quarterly reporting desk
rows.period: Quarters covering the gap reporting period
rows.account: CVN-79 equipment procurement funding line, general equipment
rows.hypothesis: The supporting BSO carrying financial-reporting responsibility is determined by which BSO funded the CVN-79 equipment procurement, not by which PEO holds lifecycle responsibility; the gap conflates the two. The funding BSO retains reporting until formal transfer, so the accountable office whose records must be reconciled is the funding BSO's, with the PEO reporting through it.

rows.instruction: Ask ASN (FM&C) Financial Reporting and NAVSEA 01 for any written allocation-of-reporting-responsibility memorandum or MOA covering CVN-79 equipment across funding BSOs for the gap period; check the PMS 378 program file and the NAVSEA property office correspondence file. Cheap kill: if the equipment is single-BSO funded, the joint-funding clause never engages.
rows.target_document: Written allocation-of-reporting-responsibility memorandum / inter-BSO MOA for CVN-79 equipment
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) Financial Reporting; NAVSEA 01 Command Property Office
rows.period: Gap reporting period and the fiscal year of initial equipment receipt
rows.account: CVN-79 equipment, multi-appropriation funding
rows.hypothesis: CVN-79 equipment is jointly funded (shipbuilding appropriation plus separate equipment or OPN/WPN lines, or shared with other carrier programs), which under the reference requires a written allocation of reporting responsibility. The absence of that written allocation is what leaves the accountable office unidentifiable, rather than any ambiguity in the instruction.

rows.instruction: Request from PMS 378 the GFP attachment/property clause listing for the CVN-79 construction contract and the PIEE GFP module property records for the gap period; identify the named government accountable property officer of record and whether an APSR accountable record exists for equipment physically at the shipbuilder. Kill if a government APSR record with a named government APO already exists for every line in question.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 construction contract GFP attachment and property clauses; PIEE GFP module property records
rows.target_system: PIEE GFP module and the designated DON APSR
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) property administration; NAVSEA Command Property Officer
rows.period: Gap reporting period
rows.account: CVN-79 GFP / contractor-acquired-turned-GFP equipment
rows.hypothesis: The equipment in question is held by the shipbuilder as government-furnished property or is contractor-acquired property delivered and accepted on the construction contract, and the dossier has been treating the contractor's property system as the system of record. Under the reference, a contractor system does not substitute for the government APSR, and the accountable record remains with the government APO — who cannot be a contractor — so the office to reconcile is the government APO, not the shipyard property organization.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-79 CIP project records in the designated APSR and the PMS 378 annual CIP-to-contract-progress reconciliation and quarterly CIP cost reviews for the gap period; obtain any transfer documentation and check whether it states that ownership and full financial reporting moved or only custody moved. Kill if a completed, relieved CIP project with matching cost/receipt/transfer documents is on file.
rows.target_document: APSR CIP project file for CVN-79 equipment; PMS 378 CIP reconciliation and quarterly review records; transfer documentation
rows.target_system: Designated DON APSR integrated with the core financial system
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378); ASN (FM&C) representative performing quarterly APSR-to-general-ledger reconciliation
rows.period: Annual CIP reconciliation and the four quarters of the gap period
rows.account: Construction-in-progress account for CVN-79 equipment
rows.hypothesis: Accountability is unassignable in the dossier because the equipment sits in a construction-in-progress posture that was never relieved: the CIP project for CVN-79 equipment has not had cost, receipt, and transfer documents reconciled in the APSR, so no post-completion transfer of ownership and reporting responsibility has been documented and the PEO's annual CIP-to-contract-progress reconciliation is the missing artifact.

rows.instruction: Obtain the current ASN (FM&C)-approved APSR list (maintained with the DON Office of the Chief Management Officer) and the CNO determination of APSRs authorized for Navy equipment management; compare against the system actually carrying the CVN-79 equipment records, and inspect the UII/local-tag fields on those records. Then pull the BSO's quarterly accountable-equipment asset list submitted to ASN (FM&C) and test whether the CVN-79 lines trace to the general-ledger ending balance. Cheapest kill in the set: a single look at the approved-APSR list against the system name.
rows.target_document: ASN (FM&C)-approved APSR list and CNO APSR determination; BSO quarterly accountable-equipment asset list
rows.target_system: Candidate APSR carrying CVN-79 equipment records
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) with DON Office of the Chief Management Officer; CNO staff
rows.period: Quarterly submissions for the gap period
rows.account: General equipment, CVN-79 hull equipment records
rows.hypothesis: The reconciliation cannot be sourced because the CVN-79 equipment is recorded in a system that is not on the ASN (FM&C)-approved APSR list, or is recorded under an identifier that does not populate the prescribed APSR fields (existing UII versus local tag), so the asset list the BSO derives for quarterly submission does not tie to the general-ledger balance and no office appears as accountable.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the FY 2007 National Defense Authorization Act split-funding authority and its detailed terms be obtained to establish what funding scope that authority permitted for the carrier construction?
rows.target_document: Public statute text / Navy Office of Legislative Affairs
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the enacted public law text and statutory notes for the FY 2007 NDAA ship-construction authorization section (and the subsequent NDAA section that extended the carrier full-funding period, plus the FY 2019 NDAA two-carrier procurement section) from the U.S. Code / Statutes at Large as codified, and compare the carrier hull numbers and fiscal-year ranges each names against the hull and years asserted in the gap statement. Kill the hypothesis if the FY 2007 text alone names CVN-79 and the full year range claimed.
rows.target_document: Enacted NDAA public law text / Statutes at Large / codified Title 10 ship-construction authorization notes
rows.target_office: Navy Office of Legislative Affairs
rows.period: FY 2007 NDAA as enacted, plus all later amending NDAA sections through FY 2019
rows.account: Carrier Replacement Program (CVN-79) hull construction authorization
rows.hypothesis: The authority at issue is not an FY 2007 NDAA provision at all, or not solely one: the inherited label 'FY 2007 NDAA split-funding authority' arrived with the question (attributed in the dossier to 'Public statute text / Navy Office of Legislative Affairs' as named executor) and may conflate the original four-year incremental-funding authorization for the named carriers with the later statutory extension of the full-funding period, and with the separate FY 2019 two-ship procurement authority. Testing the label is cheaper than reconstructing scope from it.

rows.instruction: Read the operative subsections of the FY 2007 NDAA carrier authorization for any account or line-item designation, then cross-read the CVN 78 subprogram funding-source table (carrier-replacement procurement line 2001, its two program elements, and the separate outfitting procurement line) in the program SAR/MSAR funding-source annex. Kill if the statute names appropriation accounts explicitly.
rows.target_document: FY 2007 NDAA operative subsections; CVN 78 class SAR/MSAR funding-source table
rows.target_office: Navy Office of Legislative Affairs; CVN 78 Program Office (PMS 378)
rows.period: FY 2007 through the end of the authorized full-funding period
rows.account: SCN carrier-replacement procurement line 2001 and the separate outfitting procurement line
rows.hypothesis: The statute's split-funding authority specifies an authorized funding period in years but does not itself allocate scope to specific appropriation accounts or hulls; the scope question is answerable only from the appropriation acts and the program's funding-source table, not from the authorization. If the statute is silent on account-level scope, the document request as framed cannot close the gap and must be reframed.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the NDAA section that extended the CVN-79 full-funding period from four to five years, and the still-later section extending the period covering CVN-79 and CVN-80, and record the effective fiscal-year span each establishes for CVN-79 construction. Kill if no amending section altering the CVN-79 period exists in the enacted text.
rows.target_document: Amending NDAA sections to the carrier full-funding authority
rows.target_office: Navy Office of Legislative Affairs
rows.period: FY 2008 through FY 2019 NDAAs, amending sections only
rows.account: CVN-79 hull construction (SCN)
rows.hypothesis: The authorized funding period for CVN-79 was lengthened after FY 2007, so any scope derived from the FY 2007 text understates which appropriation years legitimately carry hull construction cost; the controlling year range is set by the later amendment, not the original authority.

rows.instruction: Compare the appropriation-year span recorded in the program's acquisition estimate (PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate, noting its four-carrier procurement quantity and that class-level totals are not CVN-79 hull totals) against the statutory span, and check whether any appropriation year outside the statutory span carries CVN-79 construction cost. Kill if every year with recorded construction cost already falls inside the statutory span.
rows.target_document: PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition program estimate / SAR cost section
rows.target_system: Navy budget justification (SCN) and SAR repository
rows.target_office: CVN 78 Program Office (PMS 378)
rows.period: PB 2025 budget position
rows.account: CVN 78 class acquisition estimate, procurement quantity four
rows.hypothesis: The gap is already closable at zero residual exposure because the question is a document-availability question, not a cost question: the stated exposure is nil, suggesting the authority's scope has no unallocated dollars attached and the request is corroborative. The hypothesis is that retrieval adds documentation but changes no allocation.

rows.instruction: Request the June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification document and the shipbuilder's revised construction-preparation cost/progress baseline from the CVN 78 Program Office contracts file, and identify which scope crossed from post-shakedown availability into the construction contract and in which appropriation year it was funded. Kill if the modification moved no funded scope across appropriation years.
rows.target_document: June 2023 CVN-79 DD&C contract modification; revised construction-preparation EVM baseline
rows.target_office: CVN 78 Program Office (PMS 378) contracting file / NAVSEA 02
rows.period: June 2023 modification and subsequent baseline revision
rows.account: CVN-79 detail design and construction contract; construction-preparation contract
rows.hypothesis: Scope attributed to the split-funding authority may be contaminated by contract actions that moved work between phases and ships after enactment, so the statutory scope and the recorded construction scope will not reconcile without adjusting for those actions (post-shakedown work moved into construction, construction-preparation metrics revised for the delivery-strategy change).

rows.instruction: Query the CSDR compliance record for the CVN 78 program in the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise for the reporting period carrying the Red rating, and request from the milestone decision authority's files the status of the acquisition-program-baseline change associated with the transmitted schedule deviation report. Kill if the APB change was executed and CSDR compliance had been reassessed for the period in question.
rows.target_document: CSDR compliance assessment; schedule deviation report and APB change package
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE / Milestone Decision Authority (ASN RD&A)
rows.period: reporting period of the Red CSDR rating through the planned APB change
rows.account: CVN 78 program CSDR compliance; acquisition program baseline
rows.hypothesis: Even if the statute is obtained, the program's reported cost data cannot be mapped to statutory funding years with confidence because the program's Cost and Software Data Reporting compliance is rated Red with only an anticipated future improvement, and the baseline-change action supporting the schedule deviation remained planned rather than executed.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can EMALS Acquisition Program Baseline Change 3 and the original-baseline risk documentation be obtained to establish how the EMALS baseline was qualified and what cost scope it carried?
rows.target_document: NAVAIR PMA 251 program office / Milestone Decision Authority baseline files
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the NAVAIR PMA 251 program office acquisition document control register for the EMALS subprogram, requesting the APB revision log (original through Change 3) with distribution statements and classification markings for each revision; note whether Change 3 is recorded as signed, planned, or pending MDA signature. The mechanism describing a deviation report sent to the MDA with the associated APB change still planned makes this a one-call kill: if Change 3 is unsigned, no document can be produced and the gap closes as 'does not yet exist'.
rows.target_document: EMALS Acquisition Program Baseline revision log and APB Change 3
rows.target_system: Program office acquisition document control register
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA 251 / Milestone Decision Authority baseline files
rows.period: original baseline through the most recent APB change
rows.account: EMALS major subprogram acquisition program baseline
rows.hypothesis: The documents are not missing but simply not public: APB Change 3 and the original EMALS baseline risk documentation exist as MDA-held controlled acquisition records, and the gap is an access-control condition rather than a document-existence condition. The question's framing as obtainable is itself the inherited assumption to test.

rows.instruction: Pull the EMALS section of the Selected Acquisition Report / MSAR cost-estimate narrative for the original baseline year and read the estimate-preparation basis statement; confirm whether the estimate was prepared to Enhanced SAR guidelines and whether a risk statement was accordingly furnished. Kill cheaply by reading one narrative paragraph rather than by filing a records request.
rows.target_document: MSAR/SAR EMALS cost-estimate basis narrative
rows.target_system: Defense Acquisition Visibility Environment (DAMIR/Advana SAR repository)
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA 251 cost estimating / Navy CAPE liaison
rows.period: original baseline year
rows.account: EMALS subprogram original baseline cost estimate
rows.hypothesis: There is no original-baseline risk statement to retrieve, because the original EMALS baseline's cost estimate was not prepared to the guidelines that would require one. The retrieval request presumes a document class the baseline never produced.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the acquisition decision memorandum or MDA correspondence that designated EMALS a major subprogram, from the Milestone Decision Authority baseline files, and compare its effective date against the recorded LRIP decision date for the CVN 78 program. Check the quantity fields in the EMALS subprogram quantity table for the same reporting year.
rows.target_document: Acquisition Decision Memorandum establishing EMALS as a major subprogram
rows.target_system: MDA acquisition decision memorandum file series
rows.target_office: Milestone Decision Authority baseline files
rows.period: subprogram establishment date versus LRIP decision date
rows.account: EMALS subprogram quantity and milestone record
rows.hypothesis: The EMALS baseline qualification is already recoverable from the subprogram-establishment record without obtaining the APB itself: the baseline that established EMALS as a major subprogram was set after the LRIP decision, so the baseline carries no LRIP quantity and its cost scope is production-and-procurement scoped only. Establishing scope from the establishment record may make the APB retrieval unnecessary.

rows.instruction: Obtain the CVN-81 EMALS/AAG production contract award documentation and the program manager's estimated-price worksheet from NAVAIR PMA 251 contracts, and trace which contract line item numbers are mapped to the EMALS subprogram procurement account versus the AAG account for the award year. Confirm whether an EMALS-only obligation breakout exists in the contract writing system.
rows.target_document: CVN-81 EMALS/AAG production contract award file and PM estimated-price worksheet
rows.target_system: Electronic Document Access / Navy contract writing system
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA 251 contracting officer
rows.period: CVN-81 single-shipset contract award year through current reporting year
rows.account: EMALS procurement, CVN-81 shipset
rows.hypothesis: The cost scope the baseline carries cannot be read as EMALS-only from contract records, because the production contract that sets the procurement scope bundles EMALS with AAG while the program manager's price reflects only the EMALS production funding. The APB may therefore be retrievable yet still not separate subprogram cost from the combined-contract scope.

rows.instruction: Verify the cognizant baseline custodian by reading the signature and distribution blocks of the most recent EMALS APB change and the funding-source table attribution in the SAR supplement, which lists carrier-replacement procurement line 2001 under both the CVN 78 subprogram and the EMALS subprogram; then confirm custody with ASN(RD&A) acquisition records and PEO Aircraft Carriers before refiling the request. Source of the PMA 251 attribution: the gap record's NAMED EXECUTOR field.
rows.target_document: EMALS APB change signature and distribution pages; SAR supplement funding-source table
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A) / PEO Aircraft Carriers, cross-checked against NAVAIR PMA 251
rows.period: most recent reporting year
rows.account: Carrier-replacement procurement line 2001, EMALS subprogram
rows.hypothesis: The named executor label is wrong or incomplete: the baseline files for an EMALS major subprogram of a shipbuilding ACAT ID program may be held by the Navy acquisition executive or PEO Aircraft Carriers rather than solely by NAVAIR PMA 251, so a request addressed to PMA 251 will return nothing. This attribution arrived with the question and has not been tested.

rows.instruction: Read the original-baseline unit-cost comparison table and the quantity footnotes in the CVN 78 subprogram SAR section alongside the PB 2025 acquisition estimate quantity basis, and record the quantity used for the original baseline versus the current estimate for both the CVN 78 and EMALS subprograms. No records request required; this is a table read in the existing report.
rows.target_document: SAR/MSAR unit-cost comparison table and quantity footnotes
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA 251 cost estimating
rows.period: original baseline versus PB 2025 current estimate
rows.account: CVN 78 subprogram and EMALS subprogram unit-cost comparison
rows.hypothesis: Even with APB Change 3 in hand, the original-to-current baseline comparison will not separate EMALS cost from hull cost, because the baseline comparison rests on differing program quantities and class-level procurement quantities that are not hull totals. The retrieval would succeed and the blocked task would remain blocked, which reframes the gap as a normalization problem rather than a document problem.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the April 2015 Department of the Navy Service Cost Position memorandum and the CAPE 2020 operating and support cost-element structure guidance be obtained to establish the independent estimate's scope and to map indirect support across the 2015 and current estimates?
rows.target_document: NAVSEA 05C / NCCA (Naval Center for Cost Analysis)
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the MSAR/SAR O&S section source citation line and the NAVSEA 05C estimate transmittal log identifying which estimate populates the 'current estimate' column for the EMALS subprogram, covering the 2023 and 2024 reporting cycles, for the O&S cost-element accounts; confirm whether the cited basis is the 2023 program-office estimate or an independent estimate.
rows.target_document: MSAR/SAR O&S comparison table source citation and NAVSEA 05C estimate transmittal record
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 05C
rows.period: 2023-2024 reporting cycles
rows.account: EMALS subprogram O&S cost elements (current-estimate column)
rows.hypothesis: The two named artifacts are not the governing documents for the comparison at all: the 'current estimate' in the O&S comparison is a 2023 program-office estimate rather than the 2015 independent cost estimate, so the scope question should be directed at the 2023 PO estimate documentation rather than the April 2015 Service Cost Position memorandum. If so, obtaining the 2015 SCP memo would not close the gap.

rows.instruction: Request from NCCA the EMALS O&S cost-element crosswalk worksheet mapping legacy element 6.0 (Indirect Support) to the post-2015 CAPE structure, for the 2015 estimate and the 2024 current estimate, limited to the indirect-support account; a single crosswalk tab either exists or does not.
rows.target_document: EMALS O&S cost-element crosswalk worksheet / estimate backup file
rows.target_office: NCCA (Naval Center for Cost Analysis)
rows.period: 2015 estimate vs 2024 current estimate
rows.account: O&S cost element 6.0, Indirect Support
rows.hypothesis: The gap is closable without either named document, because the missing comparability item is specifically the omission of indirect-support element 6.0 from the current comparison table; a crosswalk of element 6.0 between the old and new CAPE structures, held as a working file by the estimating office, would establish like-for-like mapping.

rows.instruction: Search the NCCA and ASN(RD&A) cost-position correspondence register for calendar year 2015 for any Service Cost Position or independent-estimate memorandum naming EMALS or the CVN 78 class; compare title, signature authority and date against the label in the question, for the EMALS O&S and life-cycle accounts.
rows.target_document: 2015 cost-position correspondence register entry and the underlying memorandum
rows.target_office: NCCA and ASN(RD&A) cost-position signatory file
rows.period: calendar year 2015
rows.account: EMALS / CVN 78 class O&S and life-cycle estimate accounts
rows.hypothesis: INHERITED LABEL: the artifact described in the question as an 'April 2015 Department of the Navy Service Cost Position memorandum' may be mislabeled as to type, date, or originating authority — the 2015 EMALS O&S basis may be a CAIG/independent life-cycle estimate or an Enhanced-SAR-deficient baseline product rather than a DON SCP memo. The label arrived with the question and no cited source asserts it.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the OSD CAPE Operating and Support Cost-Estimating Guide / cost-element structure issuance dated 2020 from the CAPE publications index, and confirm its element-numbering table covers the indirect-support element; no Navy access request needed.
rows.target_document: OSD CAPE O&S cost-element structure guidance, 2020 edition
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE
rows.period: 2020 guidance edition
rows.account: O&S cost-element structure (all elements, incl. indirect support)
rows.hypothesis: The CAPE 2020 O&S cost-element structure guidance is publicly releasable or already distributed as an OSD issuance, so the access-required designation attaches only to the Navy-internal 2015 memorandum; the structural half of the question can be closed at near-zero cost.

rows.instruction: Compare the PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition/O&S exhibit quantity and line-item structure against the 2015 estimate's stated quantity and line structure, using the Navy budget justification supplement's funding-source table for procurement line 2001 and the outfitting line, for the PB 2025 position.
rows.target_document: Navy budget justification supplement funding-source table and PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate exhibit
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 / Navy budget office
rows.period: PB 2025 position vs 2015 estimate
rows.account: Carrier-replacement procurement line 2001 and outfitting line; O&S budget lines executed by Program/Sustainment Office
rows.hypothesis: Even with both documents in hand the comparison remains non-like-for-like for reasons other than the CAPE structure change — notably quantity and budget-position differences (four-carrier class quantity, outfitting as a separate procurement line, program-office/sustainment-office execution rather than hull-specific costing) — so the retrieval would not by itself permit attributing differences to the hull.

rows.instruction: Obtain the antecedent-estimate appendix and VAMOSC data pull parameters supporting the 2015 CVN 78 class O&S estimate, specifying whether forward-deployed ships were excluded and whether the new-construction berthing adjustment was applied, for the manpower and indirect-support accounts of the 2015 estimate.
rows.target_document: 2015 O&S estimate antecedent-data appendix and VAMOSC query documentation
rows.target_office: NCCA / NAVSEA 05C
rows.period: 2015 estimate basis year
rows.account: CVN 68 antecedent manpower and indirect-support O&S elements; new-construction berthing adjustment
rows.hypothesis: The 2015 estimate's O&S baseline rests on CVN 68 antecedent data whose source conventions differ from the current estimate (VAMOSC full-year data excluding forward-deployed ships; authorized billets at OSD composite rates), so the documents named in the question are insufficient and the antecedent-data appendix must also be obtained before any indirect-support mapping is valid.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the CVN-79 EMALS long-lead-time-material contract and the subsequent EMALS shipset contract records be obtained to establish whether their reported amounts overlap or are additive for this hull?
rows.target_document: NAVAIR PMA 251 contracting officer / contract files
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull from NAVAIR PMA-251 contract files the award document and all modifications for the CVN-79 EMALS long-lead-time-material contract and for the CVN-79 EMALS shipset contract; read the shipset contract's Section B/CLIN structure and the 'prior/related contracts' and consideration blocks for language incorporating, superseding or crediting the LLTM effort. Cheapest single check: the SF-30/SF-26 cross-reference block on the shipset award.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 EMALS LLTM award + CVN-79 EMALS shipset award and modification file
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA-251 contracting officer / procuring contracting officer contract files
rows.period: LLTM award date through shipset award and all subsequent mods
rows.account: Aircraft Procurement, Navy / Other Procurement, Navy EMALS procurement line as cited on the awards
rows.hypothesis: The two records are sequential phases of one acquisition line, not two independent buys: the LLTM award was placed first and the later shipset award (or a modification to it) subsumes or definitizes the LLTM scope, so reported amounts are partially overlapping rather than additive.

rows.instruction: In FPDS-NG / EDA, retrieve the base award and PIIN/modification history for the EMALS shipset contract cited in the MSAR EMALS procurement-deviation narrative; confirm from the award's line-item structure whether it covers CVN-79 and CVN-80 shipsets jointly. Then compare to the MSAR deviation narrative that asserted the CVN-79/80 two-shipset arrangement. Kill cheap: one FPDS record view.
rows.target_document: MSAR EMALS procurement baseline deviation narrative vs. base award document
rows.target_system: FPDS-NG and EDA (Electronic Document Access) contract award records
rows.period: CVN-79/80 two-shipset award period through most recent modification
rows.account: EMALS subprogram procurement
rows.hypothesis: The question's premise that two distinct CVN-79 contracts exist as separable records is an inherited label; what is actually in force is a two-shipset CVN-79/80 contract (and a separate CVN-81 single-shipset contract), so 'the CVN-79 EMALS shipset contract' is a hull-level description of a multi-hull instrument and cannot be read as a CVN-79-only amount.

rows.instruction: Request from PMA-251 the program manager's estimated-price worksheet underlying the MSAR contract table entries for the EMALS contracts, and identify for each row whether the figure is contract face value, obligated value, or PM estimated EMALS-only price, and whether AAG content is excluded. Check the MSAR contract-table footnotes first.
rows.target_document: MSAR contract table and its footnotes; PMA-251 PM estimated-price backup worksheet
rows.target_office: NAVAIR PMA-251 business financial manager
rows.period: MSAR reporting year covering the EMALS contracts
rows.account: EMALS production and pre-production funding lines
rows.hypothesis: The 'overlap' is an artifact of mixed reporting bases rather than of the contracts: the amounts arriving with the question come from a program-manager estimated price for a combined EMALS/AAG instrument where only the EMALS portion is reflected, so comparing that figure to a contract face value double- or under-counts scope.

rows.instruction: Read the SAR/MSAR funding-source table rows for procurement line 2001 under both the CVN 78 subprogram and the EMALS subprogram, and identify whether the same line and program elements carry EMALS content in both places; then ask NAVSEA PMS 378 / PMA-251 financial management which subprogram records the CVN-79 shipset obligation of record.
rows.target_document: SAR/MSAR funding-source table, procurement line 2001 rows (CVN 78 subprogram and EMALS subprogram)
rows.target_office: PMS 378 and PMA-251 financial management
rows.period: Current MSAR reporting year
rows.account: Carrier Replacement Program procurement line 2001; outfitting procurement line
rows.hypothesis: No double counting is possible at the hull level because the records are keyed to procurement lines and program elements, not to hulls: EMALS content is reported under a carrier-replacement procurement line shared with the CVN 78 subprogram, so 'EMALS content in hull cost' is an allocation question answerable only from the funding-source table, not from the two contract records.

rows.instruction: Query the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise (CADE) CSDR submission status for the CVN-79 EMALS LLTM and shipset contracts, and obtain the DCARC/CSDR plan and compliance correspondence cited in the MSAR Red rating; confirm whether contractor cost data reports were ever accepted for the LLTM contract. Single CADE status query kills this.
rows.target_document: CSDR plan and compliance correspondence underlying the MSAR Red rating
rows.target_system: CADE / DCARC CSDR submission and compliance records
rows.target_office: DCARC; PMA-251 cost chief
rows.period: From LLTM award through current reporting year
rows.account: EMALS subprogram contractor cost data reporting
rows.hypothesis: The contract records as held will not resolve additivity because cost reporting against them is deficient: CSDR compliance is rated Red, so contractor cost reports that would reconcile LLTM scope against shipset scope may not exist in usable form for the CVN-79 awards.

rows.instruction: Compare the EMALS subprogram original-baseline documentation (APB establishing EMALS as a major subprogram) against the PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate, recording the procurement quantity assumed in each and whether CVN-79 is carried as a follow-on ship whose current estimate updates only on divergence from the lead ship. Obtain both from the OSD AIR/SAR repository.
rows.target_document: EMALS subprogram original Acquisition Program Baseline and PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate exhibit
rows.target_office: OSD(A&S) Acquisition Information Repository / Navy SAR preparer
rows.period: Original EMALS baseline date and PB 2025 budget position
rows.account: EMALS subprogram procurement; CVN 78 subprogram acquisition estimate
rows.hypothesis: Any apparent overlap is a restated-baseline effect, not a contract effect: the EMALS baseline was established as a major subprogram without an Enhanced SAR-compliant estimate and with original-baseline-versus-current-estimate comparisons drawn on different quantities and budget positions, so amounts attached to 'this hull' were derived from differing quantity bases.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the Navy policy governing the new-construction berthing adjustment in the CVN 78 class acquisition O&M budget estimate be obtained to establish that adjustment's scope and whether any portion is hull-attributable?
rows.target_document: OPNAV N9 / ASN (FM&C) budget policy
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the MSAR/SAR supplement O&S section for the CVN 78 class (PB 2025 budget position) and read verbatim the line item and footnote text that carries the berthing adjustment; record whether the text names a governing Navy policy instruction by number or only an executing office, and whether the line is keyed to the four-carrier class quantity rather than a single hull.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class MSAR supplement, O&S/O&M budget-line narrative and footnotes
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers / CVN 78 program office SAR preparer
rows.period: PB 2025 submission, as-of date of the most recent MSAR
rows.account: CVN 78 class acquisition O&M / O&S estimate line carrying the berthing adjustment
rows.hypothesis: The "new-construction berthing adjustment" label is itself untested: the adjustment line in the CVN 78 class acquisition O&M estimate may be the SAR/supplement's generic Program-Office/Sustainment-Office-executed O&S budget line (crew berthing/habitability during construction and fitting out), not a discrete policy-governed hull charge. The label arrived with the question via the SAR supplement's O&M narrative, and no source asserts hull attribution.

rows.instruction: Query the ASN (FM&C) Financial Management Policy Manual (NAVSO P-1000) and the OPNAV instruction index for berthing/habitability of ship's force during new construction, for the fiscal years covering the PB 2025 formulation cycle; confirm or rule out an instruction number cited in the estimate's backup.
rows.target_document: NAVSO P-1000 / OPNAV instruction governing crew berthing during new construction
rows.target_office: ASN (FM&C) budget policy; OPNAV N9 resource sponsor
rows.period: FY 2023 through FY 2025 budget formulation guidance
rows.account: O&M,N operating-and-support lines executed by Program Office or Sustainment Office
rows.hypothesis: The governing document exists but is a Navy habitability/berthing-during-construction instruction or an ASN (FM&C) budget-formulation guidance paragraph that is unclassified and already citable, so the gap is a citation-location problem rather than an access problem.

rows.instruction: Compare the quantity basis stated in the PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate header against the quantity basis of the berthing adjustment's backup worksheet; request from the CVN 78 program office the exhibit showing whether the adjustment is distributed per hull or held at class level.
rows.target_document: PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate quantity/basis exhibit and adjustment backup
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers cost estimating / NCCA
rows.account: CVN 78 class acquisition estimate, O&M portion, four-carrier quantity basis
rows.hypothesis: The adjustment is class-wide, not hull-attributable, because it is sized against a four-carrier procurement quantity and against class-wide performance/support assumptions; any apportionment to a single hull would be an analyst construction, not a budgeted fact.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the 2023 program-office O&S estimate documentation used as the current estimate in the MSAR O&S comparison and trace the berthing/habitability element to its data source; verify whether it draws on VAMOSC full-year data and authorized-billet/OSD composite-rate methodology inherited from the CVN 68 antecedent.
rows.target_document: 2023 CVN 78 program-office O&S estimate backup and VAMOSC extracts
rows.target_office: NAVSEA cost engineering / Navy VAMOSC program office
rows.period: 2023 program-office O&S estimate as reported in the current MSAR
rows.account: O&S manpower / habitability element, antecedent CVN 68 comparison
rows.hypothesis: The adjustment traces to the antecedent CVN 68 O&S estimating methodology rather than to any new-construction policy: its manpower/habitability basis may be authorized billets and OSD composite rates drawn from VAMOSC, which would place it outside hull acquisition cost entirely.

rows.instruction: Cross-check the MSAR supplement's military-construction project list (West Coast homeporting, NAS North Island) and the CVN 78 funding-source table against the O&M berthing adjustment line; determine whether the adjustment duplicates or offsets a MILCON or outfitting procurement line separate from carrier-replacement line 2001.
rows.target_document: MSAR supplement MILCON project list and CVN 78 funding-source table
rows.target_office: OPNAV N9 / NAVFAC shore requirements
rows.period: Most recent MSAR reporting period and PB 2025
rows.account: MILCON homeporting project vs. outfitting procurement line vs. O&M berthing adjustment
rows.hypothesis: The berthing adjustment is in fact a homeporting/shore-infrastructure cost that migrated into the O&M estimate, in which case the governing document is a MILCON or homeporting authority rather than a berthing policy, and it is not hull-attributable.

rows.instruction: Obtain the June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification documentation and the associated revised construction-preparation cost/progress metrics, and check the deviation report sent to the milestone decision authority for whether the berthing funding responsibility was restated as part of the delivery-strategy change; absence of any policy citation there kills the standing-policy reading.
rows.target_document: June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification and schedule deviation report to the MDA
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers contracting officer; milestone decision authority staff
rows.period: June 2023 modification through the subsequent baseline-change reporting
rows.account: CVN-79 detail design and construction / post-shakedown availability work scope
rows.hypothesis: No written policy governs the adjustment as a standing rule; it was a one-time estimate adjustment tied to the CVN-79 delivery-strategy change that moved post-shakedown work into construction and shifted the delivery date, which would alter when ship's force berthing is funded and by whom.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the CVN-79 Program Deviation Report and the subsequent acquisition program baseline change be obtained to establish the approved schedule baseline and any associated cost baseline change?
rows.target_document: PEO Aircraft Carriers program office / Milestone Decision Authority correspondence file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) Milestone Decision Authority correspondence file for the CVN-79 Program Deviation Report transmittal and for any subsequent signed APB revision page, covering the period from the June 2023 contract modification through the most recent MSAR reporting date; ask specifically whether an approved, signed APB exists or whether a revision is still in staffing.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 Program Deviation Report and any subsequent APB revision
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers / PMS 378, Milestone Decision Authority correspondence file
rows.period: June 2023 through latest MSAR reporting date
rows.account: CVN-79 acquisition program baseline (schedule and cost sections)
rows.hypothesis: No acquisition program baseline change document exists yet to be obtained, because the schedule Program Deviation Report was transmitted to the Milestone Decision Authority while the associated APB revision remained only planned. In that case the gap is unclosable as framed, and only the deviation report itself (plus any MDA acknowledgment) is retrievable.

rows.instruction: Request from PMS 378 the deviation report's breach-type declaration block and the June 2023 modification's scope narrative; compare against the APB cost threshold/objective entries in the then-current baseline to confirm whether any cost parameter was declared breached.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 Program Deviation Report, breach declaration section
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers / PMS 378
rows.period: June 2023 modification through current baseline
rows.account: APB schedule thresholds vs. APB cost thresholds, CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The deviation is schedule-only: the reported breach arises from the delivery-date adjustment and the shift of post-shakedown availability work into construction, with no accompanying cost-baseline change. The 'associated cost baseline change' named in the question is an assumption carried into the gap rather than a documented event.

rows.instruction: Run a title-agnostic index search in the ASN(RD&A)/Defense Acquisition Visibility Environment record for CVN-79 breach correspondence for the reporting period, and separately ask PMS 378 for its document-control log listing by date rather than by title, to establish the artifact's actual title and custodian before further retrieval attempts.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 breach correspondence (title to be established)
rows.target_system: Defense Acquisition Visibility Environment / ASN(RD&A) acquisition records index
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A) Milestone Decision Authority staff
rows.period: reporting period covering the June 2023 modification
rows.account: document identification and custody, not a cost account
rows.hypothesis: INHERITED LABEL: the document is not titled or filed as a 'Program Deviation Report' and is not held by the named executor. The label and custodian arrived with the question (traceable to the MSAR narrative describing a report sent to the MDA, per mechanism M-...036825ad56cf), and the artifact may instead be a Program Deviation Notification, a Selected Acquisition Report breach annex, or correspondence held by the USD(A&S)/ASN(RD&A) decision authority staff rather than the program office.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN 78-class MSAR baseline-comparison tables for the current reporting period and extract the CVN-79 follow-on-ship current-estimate rows, noting the procurement quantity stated for the estimate and whether the follow-on current estimate was updated separately from the lead ship; confirm the quantity basis differs from the PB 2025 four-carrier class position before using any class-level row.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class MSAR / SAR baseline comparison tables
rows.period: current MSAR reporting period and PB 2025 position
rows.account: CVN 78 subprogram original baseline vs. current estimate, CVN-79 follow-on ship rows
rows.hypothesis: The baseline is retrievable but not from a deviation report at all: the approved schedule and cost baseline for CVN-79 is recorded in the current MSAR/SAR baseline comparison tables, and the gap can be closed from reporting already in hand without obtaining the restricted correspondence.

rows.instruction: Submit a formal access determination request to the PEO Aircraft Carriers FOIA/records officer naming the CVN-79 deviation report and draft APB revision for the post-June-2023 period, and obtain the written release determination and withholding basis; this resolves closability without requiring the substantive content.
rows.target_document: access determination and withholding basis for CVN-79 deviation report and draft APB
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers records/FOIA officer
rows.period: post-June 2023 through present
rows.account: records access determination, CVN-79 baseline documents
rows.hypothesis: Access is denied by classification or pre-decisional-deliberation withholding rather than by absence of the document; the deviation report and draft APB are pre-decisional MDA correspondence and will be refused to the requester regardless of existence.

rows.instruction: Obtain the CVN 78 subprogram funding-source table and the EMALS subprogram funding-source table from the current MSAR, and map procurement line 2001 program elements and the separate outfitting line to determine whether any APB cost row is reported at hull level for CVN-79; separately confirm from the MSAR EMALS deviation narrative that the deviation is attributed to the CVN-81 shipset contract structure.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class MSAR funding-source tables and EMALS subprogram deviation narrative
rows.period: current MSAR reporting period
rows.account: carrier-replacement procurement line 2001 program elements; outfitting procurement line; EMALS subprogram procurement
rows.hypothesis: Even if obtained, the APB cost baseline will not resolve hull-level cost variance for CVN-79, because the baseline's cost entries are structured class-wide and by subprogram with separate procurement and outfitting lines, and the EMALS subprogram deviation reported alongside it is driven by the separate CVN-81 single-shipset buy rather than by CVN-79 hull execution. The blocked item would remain blocked for a structural reason.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the CAPE 2014 and 2020 operating-and-support cost-element structure guidance be obtained to map Indirect Support between the 2015 independent estimate and the current estimate?
rows.target_document: OSD Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE)
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the EMALS subprogram O&S comparison table and its footnotes/source lines from the MSAR/SAR edition that supplied this question (current reporting year) and the immediately prior edition; read the column headers and estimate-source annotations to establish the preparation date and preparing office of each column before any guidance document is requested.
rows.target_document: EMALS subprogram MSAR/SAR O&S comparison table and footnotes
rows.target_office: Navy PEO Aircraft Carriers / program office (PMS 378) reporting cell
rows.period: Current MSAR reporting year and prior year
rows.account: EMALS major subprogram, O&S cost-element comparison table
rows.hypothesis: The gap is mis-specified at the source: the "current estimate" in the O&S comparison table is a 2023 program-office estimate, not the 2015 independent cost estimate, so the requested artifact pair (CAPE 2014 vs CAPE 2020 guidance) may not be the pair that actually governs the two displayed columns. The guidance vintages, not just the documents, are an inherited label.

rows.instruction: Query the analytic team's document library and the CAPE public document index for the O&S Cost Estimating Guide / CES editions covering the 2014 and 2020 timeframes; record edition date and distribution statement on each. One library lookup kills or confirms the access premise.
rows.target_document: CAPE Operating and Support Cost-Estimating Guide, editions covering 2014 and 2020
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE (document index / FOIA reading room)
rows.period: 2014 and 2020 editions
rows.account: O&S cost-element structure, elements 1.0 through 6.0
rows.hypothesis: No access request is needed because the applicable CAPE O&S cost-element structures are public-release documents already held, and the gap is a holdings failure rather than an access-required failure.

rows.instruction: Extract the full element-by-element line listing of both the 2015 independent estimate and the current estimate as printed in the EMALS O&S section, and diff the element labels; confirm whether the discrepancy is limited to the indirect-support element or extends to other elements. No external request required.
rows.target_document: EMALS subprogram O&S cost-element listings, 2015 independent estimate column and current estimate column
rows.period: 2015 estimate and current estimate as printed
rows.account: O&S cost elements, indirect support element 6.0
rows.hypothesis: The mapping can be reconstructed without obtaining either CAPE guidance document, because the omission is confined to indirect-support element 6.0 and the element rosters of both columns are recoverable from the report's own line items.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the budget supplement's O&S line descriptions for the CVN 78 class and EMALS and determine which executing office each line funds; compare that scope statement against the scope narrative attached to the 2015 independent estimate.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 class / EMALS MSAR budget supplement, operating-and-support line descriptions
rows.target_office: Program Office and Sustainment Office execution lines
rows.period: Current reporting year supplement versus 2015 independent estimate scope narrative
rows.account: Operating and support budget lines
rows.hypothesis: The two columns are non-comparable for a reason additional to the cost-element structure change — differing scope basis, such as program-office versus sustainment-office execution lines rather than hull-specific sustainment — so obtaining the guidance alone would not close the gap.
