rows.instruction: Request from NAVSEA 05C / Naval Center for Cost Analysis the element mapping and data-source documentation used for the CVN 68 antecedent O&S estimate (requirements, actual returns, VAMOSC, authorized billets, OSD composite rates) and check whether it carries an element crosswalk between the pre- and post-change structures.
rows.target_document: CVN 68 antecedent O&S estimate documentation and VAMOSC element mapping
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 05C / Naval Center for Cost Analysis (VAMOSC program office)
rows.period: 2015 estimate basis year and current estimate basis year
rows.account: Antecedent O&S elements including manpower
rows.hypothesis: The named executor label is wrong or incomplete: the artifact that reconciles the two structures is a Navy-side crosswalk (VAMOSC-based element mapping used for the antecedent estimate), not a CAPE guidance issuance, so the request is addressed to the wrong office.

rows.instruction: Compare the stated procurement/sustainment quantity and hull coverage declared for the 2015 independent estimate against the quantity declared in the PB-position acquisition estimate underlying the current estimate; read the quantity fields in the EMALS and CVN 78 subprogram cost tables side by side.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 and EMALS subprogram cost tables, quantity and budget-position fields
rows.period: 2015 independent estimate versus current PB position
rows.account: Program quantity / hull basis for O&S estimate
rows.hypothesis: Even with both structures in hand the sustainment comparison stays non-comparable because the underlying quantity or hull basis differs between the two columns (class-level multi-carrier basis versus a single-hull or subprogram basis), which the cost-element structure cannot resolve.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the April 26, 2004 CVN 21 Program Acquisition Decision Memorandum be obtained to verify the scope and quantity basis of its low-rate initial production decision?
rows.target_document: Milestone Decision Authority / USD(A&S) acquisition document repository
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN 78 class Selected Acquisition Report / MSAR 'Low-Rate Initial Production' data block and the original-baseline-versus-current-estimate unit cost page for the most recent reporting year, and record whether the LRIP entry is footnoted to a 2004 decision date and whether the unit-cost comparison uses differing program quantities for baseline and current estimate. Office: Navy PEO Carriers (PMS 378) SAR preparation file.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR/SAR, LRIP and unit-cost sections
rows.target_system: Defense Acquisition Visibility Environment (DAVE) / DAMIR archive
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers / PMS 378
rows.period: most recent MSAR reporting year
rows.account: CVN 78 subprogram, LRIP quantity and original-baseline unit cost fields
rows.hypothesis: The gap is not a missing-document gap at all: the LRIP quantity cited for the CVN 78 subprogram is a carried-forward attribute of a dated acquisition decision rather than a hull-level allocation, so the April 26, 2004 memorandum, even if obtained, would not tie any quantity basis to the CVN-79 hull. The gap would close by annotation rather than retrieval.

rows.instruction: Query the USD(A&S) acquisition document repository ADM index by program (CVN 21 / CVN 78) for all memoranda signed in calendar 2004 and capture title, signing MDA and decision event for each; compare the returned titles against the 2004 date asserted in the MSAR footnote that supplied this question. Do not request the body text in the first pass.
rows.target_document: ADM index entries, CVN 21 program
rows.target_office: Milestone Decision Authority / USD(A&S) document repository
rows.period: January–December 2004
rows.account: CVN 21/CVN 78 ADM series, calendar year 2004
rows.hypothesis: The document label itself is the error: the April 26, 2004 artifact may be an Acquisition Decision Memorandum for a Milestone B or design-maturity event rather than an LRIP decision, the date may be the signature date of a differently-scoped memorandum, and 'low-rate initial production decision' may be an inherited characterization introduced by the summary report rather than by the memorandum. Testing the label is cheaper than obtaining the memorandum.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the EMALS original acquisition program baseline approval document and the subprogram-establishment memorandum, and record the subprogram establishment date relative to the 2004 ADM date and whether the EMALS baseline carried an Enhanced SAR-compliant cost estimate. Office: PMA-251 / PEO Tactical Aircraft baseline file.
rows.target_document: EMALS original Acquisition Program Baseline and subprogram establishment memorandum
rows.target_office: PMA-251 / Milestone Decision Authority
rows.period: EMALS original baseline through subprogram establishment
rows.account: EMALS subprogram, original APB and establishment date
rows.hypothesis: The quantity in question belongs to a period when the program was reported as a single program, before EMALS was established as a separate major subprogram; the 2004 memorandum therefore cannot carry a subprogram-resolved quantity basis, which is why EMALS shows no LRIP quantity.

rows.instruction: Pull the PB 2025 CVN 78 class acquisition estimate quantity field and the class-wide performance threshold/objective page, and record the stated procurement quantity and whether any follow-on hull current estimate is reported separately from the lead ship. Office: Navy FMB / OPNAV N96 budget exhibit file.
rows.target_document: PB 2025 CVN 78 acquisition estimate exhibit
rows.target_office: Navy FMB (FMB-1) / OPNAV N96
rows.account: CVN 78 class acquisition estimate, procurement quantity
rows.hypothesis: The quantity basis sought is recoverable from a currently reported budget-position quantity rather than from the 2004 memorandum, but the two are not interchangeable: the current acquisition estimate is built on a multi-carrier procurement quantity whose class-level totals are not hull totals, so substituting it would misstate the hull tie-out the gap asks for.

rows.instruction: File a records-location query with the USD(A&S) repository custodian for the CVN 21 2004 ADM asking only for disposition status (on file / transferred to NARA / classified / not located), and in parallel pull the earliest CVN 78 APB and any program deviation report transmittals that cite a 2004 ADM as authority. Period: original baseline through first baseline revision.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 APB and deviation report transmittals citing the 2004 ADM
rows.target_system: USD(A&S) acquisition document repository records-disposition index
rows.target_office: USD(A&S) repository custodian / Milestone Decision Authority staff
rows.period: original baseline through first APB revision
rows.account: CVN 78 APB authority citations
rows.hypothesis: The memorandum is withheld or unlocatable for classification or records-retention reasons rather than nonexistent, in which case the closable action is a derivative record (the baseline change or deviation package that cites it) rather than the memorandum itself, following the pattern where a deviation report reached the MDA while the associated baseline change remained pending.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the FY 2019 two-ship procurement authorization and the associated savings certification, plus the statutory full-funding-period extensions for CVN-79 and CVN-80, and record which hulls each instrument covers and over how many funding years. Office: OPNAV N96 legislative file / Navy OGC.
rows.target_document: FY 2019 two-ship procurement authorization, savings certification, full-funding-period extension provisions
rows.target_office: OPNAV N96 / Navy Office of General Counsel (legislative)
rows.period: FY 2019 authorization through subsequent extension
rows.account: CVN-79/80/81 procurement authorization and full-funding authority
rows.hypothesis: Even if obtained, the memorandum will not discharge the exposure because the hull-level allocation the gap wants is driven by contracting events after 2004 — the two-ship authorization, the extended full-funding period and the multi-year funding split — none of which the 2004 quantity basis anticipates.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the shipbuilder provide the current integrated master schedule with advanced-construction status, and does the detail-design-and-construction contract require exportable schedule data as a deliverable that was in fact delivered?
rows.target_document: NAVSEA PMS 378 / shipbuilder contract data requirements list
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the CDRL (DD Form 1423) index and all schedule/management-data line items attached to the CVN-79 DD&C contract as awarded, plus every modification through the June 2023 modification, from the NAVSEA PMS 378 contract file held by the cognizant contracting officer (SUPSHIP Newport News). Read for a named integrated-master-schedule data item with an export/native-format requirement and a delivery frequency.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract CDRL / DD Form 1423 schedule data items
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 / SUPSHIP Newport News contracting officer
rows.period: contract award through June 2023 modification
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79 detail design and construction
rows.hypothesis: The contract data requirements list (CDRL) for the CVN-79 detail-design-and-construction contract never converted the intended exportable-schedule deliverable into a binding line item — program officials' stated intent to make the new schedule data a construction-contract deliverable was recorded as intent, not as executed contract language — so no exportable IMS can be compelled, only requested.

rows.instruction: Query the PMS 378 contract deliverable receipt log / Electronic Data Access or program document repository for receipt records against the schedule CDRL item number, listing transmittal dates, file formats and acceptance/rejection actions, for the full period of the DD&C contract.
rows.target_document: CDRL deliverable receipt and acceptance log
rows.target_system: program document repository / Electronic Data Access
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 data manager
rows.period: contract award to present
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract deliverable receipts
rows.hypothesis: The deliverable exists and was in fact delivered, but into a receiving system the reconciliation team never queried — delivered schedule files sit in the program's contract-deliverable repository unreviewed rather than being undelivered.

rows.instruction: Obtain from the shipbuilder, via PMS 378, the current list of scheduling tools and products of record for CVN-79 with the name, owner and export capability of each, and map each to the schedule product GAO examined in its CVN-79 construction-progress review. Identify which source first applied the phrase 'integrated master schedule' to this program.
rows.target_document: shipbuilder scheduling-system description / GAO CVN-79 report working papers
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: period of GAO CVN-79 construction-progress review to present
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label "integrated master schedule" is wrong for what would answer the question: GAO's finding concerned the shipbuilder's legacy master construction schedule, while the exportable artifact is a different, newer scheduling product under a different name and owner. The gap may be chasing a document that does not exist under that title.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the CVN-79 construction-preparation contract statements of work and their schedule/reporting requirements from PMS 378, and compare the work-breakdown coverage of the preparation contracts against the schedule baseline activity list under the DD&C contract for the preparation period.
rows.target_document: construction-preparation contract SOW and schedule reporting clauses
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: construction-preparation period through DD&C award
rows.account: CVN-79 construction preparation (advance procurement / long-lead material)
rows.hypothesis: An up-to-date schedule exists but structurally cannot carry advanced-construction status, because advanced construction and construction-preparation work (long-lead material, structural units) were performed under separate preparation contracts whose work is not loaded into the DD&C schedule baseline.

rows.instruction: Request the shipbuilder's documented mapping between its labor/material cost-collection system control accounts and master-construction-schedule activities for CVN-79, together with the program's Cost and Software Data Reporting compliance assessment and corrective-action plan, from PMS 378 business financial management.
rows.target_document: cost-to-schedule crosswalk / CSDR compliance assessment and CAP
rows.target_system: shipbuilder labor and material tracking system
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: current reporting period and the two prior annual reports
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C reported percent complete (dollars-based)
rows.hypothesis: Even a delivered exportable schedule would not validate the dollars-based percent complete, because labor and material are tracked in a system separate from the master construction schedule with no automatic propagation of changes; the blocker is the absent crosswalk between the two systems, not the schedule file.

rows.instruction: Obtain the June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification and any subsequent rebaselining documentation from PMS 378, reading specifically for suspension, deferral or revision of schedule-data delivery obligations and for the approved schedule baseline date in effect.
rows.target_document: June 2023 CVN-79 contract modification and rebaseline approval memoranda
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 / SUPSHIP Newport News contracting officer
rows.period: June 2023 to present
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract; post-delivery and outfitting
rows.hypothesis: Schedule content and delivery obligations were overtaken by scope moves — the June 2023 modification pulling post-shakedown work into construction and the two-phase delivery concept deferring warfare and communications work — so the current schedule of record is mid-rebaseline and no compliant deliverable is due until the rebaseline is accepted.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the Navy's FY2026 budget submission, including Table 1's annual full-funding, advance-procurement, and cost-to-complete lines for CVN-79, be obtained to verify the budget presentation underlying the reported procurement and cost-to-complete amounts?
rows.target_document: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Navy (Financial Management and Comptroller), FMB - SCN budget justification books
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Retrieve the FY2026 President's Budget SCN justification book from ASN(FM&C)/FMB public budget materials; pull the CVN-79 P-5/P-5A and P-10 exhibits under BA-1 Aircraft Carriers for FY2026 and the prior-year columns, and confirm whether advance procurement, full funding, and cost-to-complete appear as separately labeled lines for that hull.
rows.target_document: FY2026 SCN budget justification book (P-5/P-5A, P-10 exhibits for CVN-79)
rows.target_office: ASN(FM&C) FMB
rows.period: FY2026 President's Budget (with prior-year columns)
rows.account: SCN, BA-1 Aircraft Carriers, CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The gap is already closable from an unclassified public source: the FY2026 SCN budget justification book (Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy, Budget Activity 1, Aircraft Carriers, CVN-79 line) is published on the FMB public budget-materials site, and the Table 1 full-funding, advance-procurement, and cost-to-complete lines can be matched line-for-line against the SCN exhibit without any new request to the executor.

rows.instruction: Inspect the column headings and footnotes of the FY2026 SCN P-5 exhibit for CVN-79 to confirm the reported values are budget estimates in then-year dollars; then query the Navy's execution system of record (DAI/NAVY ERP and the SCN appropriation status reports to Congress) for CVN-79 obligations and outlays by appropriation year, and note whether any SCN exhibit carries an obligation or outlay column at all.
rows.target_document: SCN P-5 exhibit column definitions; Navy SCN appropriation status/execution reports
rows.target_office: ASN(FM&C) FMB and Navy budget execution (FMB-2/FMO)
rows.period: FY2013 through FY2026 appropriation years
rows.account: SCN appropriation, CVN-79 line, obligations/outlays by appropriation year
rows.hypothesis: The gap as framed is unclosable-by-design rather than unclosable-by-access: SCN exhibits report budget estimates in then-year dollars, not obligations or outlays, so obtaining them cannot by itself separate estimates from recorded execution. The reconciliation requires a second, different source and the retrieval request is mis-specified.

rows.instruction: Pull the source notes and footnotes attached to Table 1 in the originating CRS Ford-class carrier program report and identify, per column, which budget submission year and which congressional action each entry is sourced to; specifically test whether any entry is assigned to a fiscal year on the basis of congressional action rather than the Navy submission.
rows.target_document: CRS report containing Table 1 (Ford-class carrier program), source notes and footnotes
rows.target_office: originating analyst of record for the dossier's cited report
rows.period: as-published edition of the source report
rows.account: CVN-79 procurement funding history columns
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label 'Table 1' and its attribution of annual full-funding, advance-procurement and cost-to-complete amounts to the Navy's FY2026 submission is itself untested: the table may be a CRS-constructed compilation drawing on multiple budget years and congressional action, not a reproduction of any single FY2026 exhibit, in which case no single document will verify it.

rows.instruction: Compare the CVN-79 line classification in the FY2026 SCN P-5 exhibit against the FY2024 and FY2025 SCN exhibits for the same hull, and retrieve the Navy's reprogramming action documentation (DD 1415 series) covering the post-final-full-funding-year CVN-79 entry to see which classification the Navy applied.
rows.target_document: SCN P-5 exhibits FY2024-FY2026; DD Form 1415 reprogramming action for CVN-79
rows.target_office: ASN(FM&C) FMB
rows.period: FY2024-FY2026 submissions plus the governing reprogramming action
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79, cost-to-complete vs full funding classification
rows.hypothesis: The cost-to-complete line for CVN-79 is reclassified or absent in the FY2026 SCN exhibit because funding arriving after the original final full-funding year was classified as full funding under expanded incremental-funding authority, so the Table 1 label and the exhibit label will not agree even when the document is obtained.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the FY2026 OM&S/post-delivery and outfitting (PD&O) justification pages alongside the CVN-79 SCN exhibit and trace whether funds identified for post-delivery activities in the FY2025 submission appear reduced in FY2026; request the program office's schedule-change funding decision memorandum from PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378).
rows.target_document: FY2026 PD&O justification pages; PMS 378 schedule-change funding decision memo
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) and ASN(FM&C) FMB
rows.period: FY2025 and FY2026 submissions
rows.account: CVN-79 post-delivery and outfitting vs SCN hull line
rows.hypothesis: Part of the amount Table 1 attributes to new CVN-79 procurement or cost-to-complete is money previously budgeted for post-delivery activities and shifted on account of the schedule change, so the SCN exhibit will show a source-of-funds movement rather than a new procurement request, and the reconciliation line is a transfer not an increment.

rows.instruction: Obtain the Navy's statutory cost-cap compliance report / annual cap certification for CVN-79 from ASN(RD&A) and compare its scope statement against the FY2026 SCN exhibit totals, including whether GFE and excluded spares are inside or outside each figure; also retrieve any CNO capability determination and the associated congressional notification triggered by the conditional cap increase.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 cost-cap compliance certification and notification letters; SCN P-5 exhibit
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A) and ASN(FM&C) FMB
rows.period: FY2016 authorization through FY2026
rows.account: CVN-79 statutory cost cap vs SCN exhibit total; GFE/CFE split
rows.hypothesis: Amounts visible in Table 1 for CVN-79 are not comparable to the hull cost in the reconciliation because statutory cost-cap exclusions (specified spares and post-December 2018 economic inflation) and the conditional CVN-79 cap increase cause the budget presentation to carry costs outside the capped figure, so the exhibit totals and the cap-referenced figures are different scopes.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the November 2018 DoD Ford Class Aircraft Carrier Certification and its supporting GFE and shipbuilder savings estimates for the CVN-80/81 two-ship buy be obtained to identify what was excluded and which hulls were covered?
rows.target_document: OUSD(A&S) / PEO Aircraft Carriers (PEO CVN) certification file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from OUSD(A&S) correspondence control / legislative affairs the November 2018 congressional transmittal log entry for the Ford-class two-ship certification, and obtain the signed certification plus all enclosures; confirm the enclosure list names a shipbuilder savings estimate and a GFE treatment statement.
rows.target_document: November 2018 Ford Class Aircraft Carrier Certification and enclosures
rows.target_office: OUSD(A&S) legislative affairs / correspondence control
rows.period: November 2018
rows.account: CVN-80/CVN-81 two-ship block buy certification
rows.hypothesis: The November 2018 certification exists as a formal certification document transmitted by OUSD(A&S) to the congressional defense committees under the FY2019 two-ship-buy authority, and the savings estimate and its GFE exclusion appear in the certification's enclosures (cost-savings basis of estimate), making the exclusion and hull coverage readable on the face of the document.

rows.instruction: Pull the source footnote in the CRS Ford-class carrier report (and any GAO carrier report citing it) that asserts a November 2018 DoD certification, and compare the asserted title/date/signer against the PEO CVN correspondence index for Sep 2018-Feb 2019.
rows.target_document: cited certification reference in secondary reports
rows.target_office: CRS/GAO report footnotes vs. PEO CVN correspondence index
rows.period: September 2018 - February 2019
rows.account: citation provenance for the asserted certification
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label 'DoD Ford Class Aircraft Carrier Certification, November 2018' is wrong in date, signer, or title — the document may be an acquisition decision memorandum, a business-case analysis, or a certification signed in a different month or by the Navy rather than OUSD(A&S) — so retrieval is failing on the label, not on access. The label arrived with the question via the CRS/GAO carrier report citation chain rather than from the issuing office.

rows.instruction: Request from PEO CVN contracting (NAVSEA PMS 378) the CVN-80/81 block-buy contract award documentation and the pre-negotiation/price negotiation memorandum, and extract the GFE/CFE scope split and the hull line items.
rows.target_document: CVN-80/81 block-buy contract file and price negotiation memorandum
rows.target_office: PEO CVN / PMS 378 contracting
rows.period: FY2019 award
rows.account: CVN-80/CVN-81 block-buy contract scope
rows.hypothesis: Hull coverage and GFE exclusion are independently recoverable from the CVN-80/81 block-buy contract award file and its pre-award cost analysis, so the certification itself is not required to close the gap; the contract scope lines state which end items are shipbuilder-furnished versus government-furnished.

rows.instruction: Obtain from NAVSEA cost engineering (NAVSEA 05C) the two-ship-buy business case analysis and its stated baseline (separate-buy cost estimates for CVN-80 and CVN-81), and confirm whether CVN-79 appears as a cost element or only as program context.
rows.target_document: CVN-80/81 two-ship-buy business case analysis
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 05C cost engineering
rows.account: two-ship-buy savings estimate baseline
rows.hypothesis: The savings estimate is a comparison against separate-buy estimates for CVN-80 and CVN-81 and contains no CVN-79 component at all, so the reconciliation exposure is a mis-attribution risk that can be retired by reading the estimate's baseline definition rather than by obtaining the full certification.

rows.instruction: Query the GFE-providing program offices supporting Ford-class (e.g., PEO Tactical Aircraft/launch-and-recovery and NAVSEA propulsion offices) for their 2018 economic-order-quantity savings submissions prepared in support of the two-ship certification, for CVN-80 and CVN-81 end items.
rows.target_document: GFE EOQ/cross-program savings submissions supporting the certification
rows.target_office: Ford-class GFE provider program offices
rows.period: calendar 2018
rows.account: GFE economic-order-quantity savings estimates
rows.hypothesis: The GFE savings portion was estimated separately by GFE program offices (aviation, propulsion, combat systems) rather than by the shipbuilder, which is why GFE is excluded from the shipbuilder figure; those separate GFE economic-order-quantity estimates are the missing boundary document.

rows.instruction: Search the House and Senate Armed Services Committee FY2019 and FY2020 authorization hearing and report record for the submitted certification text or its summary, and separately request the classification/proprietary determination from PEO CVN security for the certification file.
rows.target_document: congressional record copy or redacted version of the certification
rows.target_office: HASC/SASC seapower records and PEO CVN security
rows.period: FY2019-FY2020 authorization cycle
rows.account: certification release status
rows.hypothesis: The certification and its estimates are classified or contractor-proprietary in whole or part, so the closable artifact is a redacted or summary version appearing in the FY2019/FY2020 congressional authorization record, and access rather than existence is the binding constraint.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can CVN-78 TEMP Revision F and the Enterprise Air Warfare TEMP 1910 be obtained to establish which CVN-79 systems differ from the lead ship's tested configuration and what tests are planned for them?
rows.target_document: DOT&E / PEO Aircraft Carriers test and evaluation office
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the DOT&E Test and Evaluation Master Plan registry and the DASD(DT&E)/DOT&E annual-report document index for Ford-class (CVN-78/79) TEMP records and for any TEMP numbered 1910 "Enterprise Air Warfare"; retrieve the approval cover page and revision history list only, for approvals dated FY2015 through FY2026. Confirm or kill the document titles, revision letters, and whether coverage is class-level or hull-level before requesting content.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 class TEMP (all revisions) and TEMP No. 1910
rows.target_office: DOT&E / DASD(DT&E) TEMP registry
rows.account: Ford-class CVN SCN program T&E documentation
rows.hypothesis: The inherited document labels are wrong: there is no "CVN-78 TEMP Revision F" and no separate "Enterprise Air Warfare TEMP 1910" as named; the CVN-79 test scope may live in a class-level Ford-class TEMP (or a DOT&E-approved annex), which under the cited guidance need not be reported per hull. The labels arrived with the question/GAO-derived gap text, not from a DOT&E index entry.

rows.instruction: Submit a document-control query to the PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) T&E lead for the distribution statement, classification caveat, and releasability determination on the Ford-class TEMP and its air-warfare annex as of the current fiscal year; request the cover/distribution page only. A restricted distribution statement kills the "obtainable by normal request" assumption immediately.
rows.target_document: Ford-class TEMP cover and distribution statement
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) T&E lead
rows.period: current FY
rows.account: CVN-79 test and evaluation
rows.hypothesis: The documents exist and are obtainable, but the blockage is classification/distribution rather than existence: combat system and radar test scope (SSDS, CEC, EASR/DBR) is held at a controlled level requiring a cleared reading-room request rather than a document pull.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the TEMP and current test-plan summary for the SSDS program of record and the CEC program of record from PEO Integrated Warfare Systems (PEO IWS 10/ IWS 2) for the period covering CVN-79 delivery preparation; look specifically for the CVN-79 platform-integration test events and who funds them. If CVN-79 events appear only there, the carrier TEMP request is the wrong door.
rows.target_document: SSDS TEMP; CEC TEMP
rows.target_office: PEO Integrated Warfare Systems
rows.account: SSDS and CEC program of record T&E
rows.hypothesis: The CVN-79-unique test scope is not in the carrier TEMP at all because SSDS and CEC are separate programs of record; their test scope sits in their own program TEMPs and the carrier document only cross-references coordination.

rows.instruction: Pull the current Ford-class Acquisition Program Baseline and the latest Selected Acquisition Report performance section from the Defense Acquisition Visibility environment / OUSD(A&S) DAES repository and check whether any CVN-79-specific performance or cost baseline line exists. Absence kills the premise that TEMP retrieval closes the attribution gap.
rows.target_document: Ford-class APB; Ford-class SAR
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers / OUSD(A&S)
rows.period: most recent approved APB and SAR
rows.account: Ford-class APB / SAR performance and cost baseline
rows.hypothesis: Even if obtained, the TEMPs will not separate CVN-79-unique work from lead-ship work in cost terms, because the program carries a single class acquisition program baseline with lead-ship thresholds applied to follow ships; test scope documents describe events, not hull-level cost attribution.

rows.instruction: Request from SUPSHIP Newport News and PMS 378 business office the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract modification log with scope descriptions for modifications adding combat system/radar configuration and trials work, FY2019 through FY2026, and cross-read against the SCN budget justification exhibit narrative lines for CVN-79 in the FY24, FY25 and FY26 submissions.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract modification log; SCN P-form justification narrative
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News / PMS 378 business office
rows.account: SCN CVN-79 detail design and construction contract line and SCN budget justification
rows.hypothesis: The CVN-79 test, trials, and retrofit work is traceable instead through contract and budget artifacts rather than T&E plans: the FY24-FY26 budget justification attributed added funding to the longer schedule and incorporation of new systems, and the FPIF contract plus its modifications would carry the discrete CVN-79 configuration scope.

rows.instruction: Request the PMS 378 configuration/backfit decision memorandum log and any pending engineering change proposals for CVN-79 covering the fourth AAG engine and F-35C capability integration, from contract award through the current fiscal year; check for an approval date. An open or absent decision record confirms the scope is undocumented rather than withheld.
rows.target_document: PMS 378 backfit/ECP decision log
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) chief engineer
rows.period: award through current FY
rows.account: CVN-79 configuration changes and backfit decisions
rows.hypothesis: Retrofit scope in question is a pending, undecided item rather than a documented test plan: the omitted fourth AAG engine and similar deferred or backfit items have no approved test scope yet, so no TEMP revision would contain them and the gap cannot be closed by document retrieval in this period.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the Ford-class Acquisition Program Baseline be obtained to determine exactly which cost measures, ship quantities, and increments it covers for CVN-79?
rows.target_document: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) program office / Milestone Decision Authority baseline file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) the cover page, program-identification block, and cost-baseline table of the currently approved Ford-class APB, and compare against the Ford-Class Selected Acquisition Report cost section for the same reporting year; read only the row/column headers to see whether the cost measure is indexed by hull (CVN-78/79/80) or by class/average unit. Headers alone decide it.
rows.target_document: Ford-class Acquisition Program Baseline; Ford-Class Selected Acquisition Report
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378)
rows.period: Most recent approved APB and the SAR of the same reporting year
rows.account: Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy (SCN) — CVN-79 line
rows.hypothesis: The document exists but is a single class-level Ford-class APB with no CVN-79-specific cost measures, so the gap closes as 'obtainable but non-responsive': the baseline covers the class, confirming the BLOCKS condition rather than resolving it.

rows.instruction: Pull the APB revision history/change log from the Milestone Decision Authority baseline file (the office of the Navy MDA for CVN programs) and list approval dates and stated quantity for each revision; check whether a revision postdating the two-ship CVN-80/81 contract changed the covered ship quantity or LRIP quantity. The question as received asserts a single baseline — verify which revision the executor holds.
rows.target_document: APB revision history / baseline change log
rows.target_office: Milestone Decision Authority baseline file (Navy acquisition executive)
rows.period: All APB revisions from Milestone B/C through the latest approval
rows.account: CVN-79 and CVN-80/81 SCN quantities as stated in the APB quantity block
rows.hypothesis: The label 'Ford-class Acquisition Program Baseline' as the correct anchor document is an inherited label: the quantity and increment coverage may actually be governed by a later APB revision reflecting the CVN-80/81 two-ship buy, so the named document is the wrong version rather than unobtainable.

rows.instruction: Send a document-availability query (not a content query) to PMS 378 records custodian asking only for the APB's distribution statement, classification marking, and controlling authority for release; a one-line answer kills or confirms the access_required framing before any content request is drafted.
rows.target_document: Ford-class APB distribution/classification cover sheet
rows.target_system: Navy records management / FOIA tracking system
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) records custodian / Navy FOIA
rows.period: Current
rows.account: N/A — document control metadata only
rows.hypothesis: Access is the only real obstacle and it is a classification/distribution-marking problem, not an existence problem: the APB is controlled and must be requested through the program office's FOIA or congressional-liaison channel, after which cost measures and increments are readable.

rows.instruction: Query the DAMIR/Acquisition Visibility program registry for any MDAP sub-program or increment registered under the Ford-class program element, and request from the MDA baseline file any Acquisition Decision Memorandum establishing a sub-program or increment. Absence of a registered sub-program entry disconfirms cheaply.
rows.target_document: Acquisition Decision Memoranda; MDAP/sub-program registration record
rows.target_office: Milestone Decision Authority baseline file
rows.period: Milestone B through present
rows.account: MDAP program registry entries under the Ford-class program element
rows.hypothesis: No separate CVN-79 baseline or increment baseline exists because the Ford class was never managed as increments or sub-programs, so the 'increments it covers' part of the question is unanswerable by construction and the proposal for per-ship baselines is a recommendation, not a record.

rows.instruction: Pull the SCN budget justification exhibits (ship-specific line for CVN-79, including the FY24 request citing schedule extension and new systems) and the CVN-79 detail design and construction fixed-price-incentive contract target/ceiling values held by SUPSHIP Newport News; determine whether these give a hull-indexed cost measure mappable to the APB's class-level measure.
rows.target_document: SCN budget justification exhibits; CVN-79 DD&C contract face sheet
rows.target_system: Navy budget exhibit library (P-forms) / EDA contract repository
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News; PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: FY24 budget submission and contract award through latest modification
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79 ship line; CVN-79 DD&C contract and construction-preparation modification
rows.hypothesis: Even if the APB is class-level for cost, a hull-level allocation already exists outside the APB in budget-exhibit and contract records, so the reconciliation anchor can be reconstructed without the APB and the BLOCKS statement is overstated.

rows.instruction: Compare the APB schedule-parameter table's delivery and IOC events against the program office's delivery-strategy change documentation and the statutory cost-cap compliance memorandum for CVN-79 held by PMS 378; check whether deferred work and post-delivery capability insertion are inside or outside the baselined scope. Read event definitions only, no values.
rows.target_document: APB schedule and performance parameter tables; CVN-79 cost-cap compliance memorandum
rows.target_system: MDA baseline file / Navy acquisition reporting
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378)
rows.period: From the delivery-strategy change through the latest APB approval
rows.account: CVN-79 cost-cap compliance scope; deferred/post-delivery work scope
rows.hypothesis: The APB's CVN-79 coverage may be scope-ambiguous rather than cost-ambiguous: whether the baseline's schedule and performance events include deferred pre-delivery work and post-delivery capability (e.g., the two-phase delivery arrangement and F-35C acceptance conditions) determines whether its cost measure is comparable to any hull figure at all.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the approved CVN-79 acquisition strategy and its shipbuilding-review tailoring documentation be obtained to identify which reviews, decision points, and reporting events actually applied to this hull?
rows.target_document: PEO Aircraft Carriers program office; ASN(RD&A) acquisition strategy approval file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) the acquisition strategy document index/configuration list for the Ford-class program covering award of the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract through the most recent revision, and ask specifically whether any document is titled or scoped to CVN-79 alone. A one-page document list kills or confirms this immediately before any approval file is pulled.
rows.target_document: Ford-class acquisition strategy document index / configuration-managed revision list
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378)
rows.period: CVN-79 DD&C award through present
rows.account: Ford-class program documentation structure
rows.hypothesis: No CVN-79-specific acquisition strategy document exists as a separate artifact; the hull is covered by a single Ford-class acquisition strategy and one class-level APB, so the requested document is class-level and the tailoring language sits inside it rather than in a hull-specific file.

rows.instruction: Query the ASN(RD&A) acquisition strategy approval file / Acquisition Decision Memorandum series for the Ford-class program for the signed approval cover memo and any tailoring determination attachment; ask the ASN(RD&A) action officer for the ADM log entries by date for the program, not the strategy body itself. Absence of an ADM log entry is a cheap kill.
rows.target_document: ASN(RD&A) Acquisition Decision Memoranda and acquisition strategy approval cover memos, Ford-class
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A)
rows.period: Milestone B/C decision window and subsequent strategy revisions
rows.account: Milestone decision authority approval record
rows.hypothesis: The approved strategy and its tailoring exist and are retrievable, but only through the milestone decision authority's approval file rather than the program office, because approval authority (not drafting) is where the signed tailoring determination resides.

rows.instruction: Pull the Milestone B and Milestone C decision documentation for the Ford-class program from the ASN(RD&A) ADM file and check whether a single combined ADM covers both; cross-check against the SAR milestone schedule page listing planned and actual decision dates for the program.
rows.target_document: Combined Milestone B/C Acquisition Decision Memorandum and SAR milestone schedule page
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A); PEO Aircraft Carriers
rows.period: Program Milestone B through Milestone C
rows.account: Milestone decision points
rows.hypothesis: The tailoring took the form of combining development and initial-production commitments and combining Milestones B and C, so the set of dated decision points for this hull is smaller than a standard program would produce, and the 'reviews that applied' question resolves to a combined-milestone ADM rather than a separate review schedule.

rows.instruction: Trace the provenance of the phrase 'shipbuilding-review tailoring documentation' in the dossier back to its source citation, then ask the PEO Aircraft Carriers acquisition management lead whether the program holds any document of that type or title; if the phrase traces only to a paraphrase of SECNAVINST/Navy acquisition guidance, the label is dead and the retrieval target must be restated.
rows.target_document: Dossier source citation for the tailoring-documentation phrase; SECNAVINST acquisition guidance section on shipbuilding tailoring
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers acquisition management lead
rows.period: Dossier assembly period
rows.account: Question-premise provenance
rows.hypothesis: The inherited premise that a discrete 'shipbuilding-review tailoring documentation' artifact exists for this hull is itself an untested label, likely carried over from the mechanism summary of Navy acquisition guidance rather than from any citation to a held document; the tailoring may be a guidance permission that was exercised without a standalone tailoring memo.

rows.instruction: Request the Ford-class Selected Acquisition Reports (and successor annual acquisition reports) for the years spanning the CVN-79 construction period from the DoD acquisition reporting repository and inspect the cost and schedule sections for any CVN-79-labeled line; simultaneously ask PEO Aircraft Carriers whether hull-level reporting was ever directed.
rows.target_document: Ford-class Selected Acquisition Reports / successor annual program reports
rows.target_office: OSD acquisition reporting repository; PEO Aircraft Carriers
rows.period: CVN-79 construction-preparation award through most recent report
rows.account: Statutory and annual program reporting
rows.hypothesis: The reporting events actually applicable to the hull are class-level SAR/SAR-successor reports with no hull-level breakout, so even a retrieved strategy will not yield CVN-79-specific reconciliation checkpoints; the checkpoints must instead be derived from contract and acceptance events.

rows.instruction: Submit a single access-determination request to the PEO Aircraft Carriers security/FOIA point of contact naming the Ford-class acquisition strategy and its approval memo, and ask SUPSHIP Newport News for the on-site holdings index of program acquisition documentation; a written withholding basis cheaply distinguishes 'restricted' from 'nonexistent'.
rows.target_document: Access/withholding determination letter; SUPSHIP Newport News program documentation holdings index
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers security/FOIA POC; SUPSHIP Newport News
rows.period: Current
rows.account: Document access and release determination
rows.hypothesis: Access is restricted rather than the document absent: the approved strategy and tailoring are controlled acquisition-sensitive or contractor-proprietary material tied to the fixed-price-incentive contract and the deferred-work/cost-cap plan, so closure depends on an access determination, not on discovery.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: How were the CVN-79 capability modifications (updated combat system, replacement radar, AAG/AWE changes) managed under SECNAVINST 5000.02G reporting provisions and DoDI 5000.80 MTA naming, reporting, and scope rules, and which program of record carries each cost?
rows.target_document: ASN(RD&A) acquisition policy office / PEO Aircraft Carriers program documentation
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the PEO Tactical Aircraft / PMA-251 (Aircraft Launch and Recovery Equipment) program office acquisition program baseline and the AAG and Advanced Weapons Elevator line-item justification sheets in the Navy FY2026 RDT&E,N and WPN/OPN budget exhibits (P-40/R-2), and compare the carrier-program GFE line in the PEO Aircraft Carriers CVN-79 SCN P-5 cost-element breakdown for FY2024-FY2026. If AAG/AWE appear as separate program-of-record lines, the hull attribution is dead in one lookup.
rows.target_document: FY2026 President's Budget P-5/P-40 and R-2 exhibits; AAG/AWE program APBs
rows.target_office: PEO Tactical Aircraft Programs (PMA-251) and PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 379)
rows.period: FY2024-FY2026 budget submissions
rows.account: SCN CVN-79 (GFE/Other Costs cost elements); RDT&E,N and WPN/OPN lines for AAG and AWE
rows.hypothesis: The label "AAG/AWE changes on CVN-79" inherited with the question is not a CVN-79 program-of-record scope item at all: AAG is managed by a separate Navy program (as it was for CVN-78, where AAG and DBR development sat outside reported carrier development costs), so the modification cost is carried in that system program's records and only the shipboard installation/GFE delivery touches the hull program. The label arrived via the CRS-style carrier report tying the revised delivery date to AAG certification and AWE work, which is a schedule statement, not a cost-attribution statement.

rows.instruction: Request the CVN-79 Acquisition Program Baseline and the signed Acquisition Decision Memoranda / tailoring approval from ASN(RD&A) acquisition policy office covering the combat system and radar replacement decisions; look specifically for whether the capability was designated an increment of the CVN-78 class program or chartered separately. Also pull the CVN-79 Selected Acquisition Report scope statement for the same years.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 APB, ADMs, and SAR scope section
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A) acquisition policy office
rows.period: From the radar replacement decision through FY2026
rows.account: CVN-79 program of record (APB cost baseline)
rows.hypothesis: The modifications were handled inside the original CVN-79 program of record rather than as separate programs, which SECNAVINST 5000.02G expressly permits; in that case all of the cost sits in the CVN-79 SCN line and the "which program of record" question resolves to the hull with no MTA involved.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the radar program (PEO Integrated Warfare Systems, IWS 2.0) acquisition documentation and its RDT&E,N and OPN budget exhibits for the CVN-79 radar variant, and cross-check the CVN-79 SAR performance-attributes annex for whether radar performance is reported as a carrier-program attribute or deferred to the radar program.
rows.target_document: PEO IWS radar program APB and FY2026 R-2/P-40 exhibits; CVN-79 SAR
rows.target_office: PEO Integrated Warfare Systems (IWS 2.0)
rows.account: Radar program RDT&E,N / OPN lines; CVN-79 SAR performance annex
rows.hypothesis: The radar replacement is carried by a separate radar program of record (the DBR-to-EASR/successor transition), not by CVN-79, because the CVN-78 precedent put DBR development outside reported carrier development costs and because CVN-79's configuration is acknowledged to differ from CVN-78's tested configuration.

rows.instruction: Query the DoD Acquisition Visibility Data Framework / DAMIR-successor MTA program registry and the ASN(RD&A) MTA designation memoranda file for any MTA charter naming CVN-79, AAG, AWE, or the carrier combat system, and obtain the associated MTA acquisition strategy with its scope and reporting section.
rows.target_document: MTA designation memoranda and MTA acquisition strategies
rows.target_office: ASN(RD&A) acquisition policy office
rows.period: FY2019 (DoDI 5000.80 issuance) through FY2026
rows.account: MTA program registry entries and their funding lines
rows.hypothesis: One or more of the modifications was chartered as a Middle Tier of Acquisition effort (rapid prototyping or rapid fielding) under DoDI 5000.80, in which case the naming, reporting and scope attention the MTA guidance demands for subprograms, spirals, increments and block upgrades is the governing document trail and the cost sits in the MTA's own reporting, outside the hull's reported baseline.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract modification log and engineering change proposal register from NAVSEA 02 (contracts) / SUPSHIP Newport News for the period covering the combat system and radar decisions, and match each ECP to a funding appropriation line.
rows.target_document: Contract modification log and ECP register
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 02 / SUPSHIP Newport News
rows.period: Award of DD&C through FY2026
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract modifications and ECPs
rows.hypothesis: The modifications were never a separately reported acquisition at all but were absorbed as engineering changes to the fixed-price-incentive detail design and construction contract, so the trail is contract modifications and change orders rather than program-of-record documentation; this is also where an apparent hull cost increase could originate without any new program scope.

rows.instruction: Request CVN-79 obligation and expenditure data by cost element from the Navy Enterprise Resource Planning system (NAVSEA financial reporting) rather than budget exhibits, for the appropriation years in question, and separately obtain the Navy's cost-cap compliance report showing which costs were excluded under the FY2016 and FY2020 authorization provisions.
rows.target_document: Navy ERP obligation/expenditure reports and cost-cap compliance notifications to Congress
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 01 (Comptroller) / PEO Aircraft Carriers business financial manager
rows.account: SCN CVN-79 obligations/expenditures by cost element; cost-cap compliance exclusions
rows.hypothesis: The question's premise of an attributable modification cost is itself untestable as posed because the available CVN-79 figures are budget estimates, cost-to-complete funding requests and then-year funding entries rather than recorded hull expenditures, and statutory cost-cap exclusions further detach reported cap figures from actual scope; there may be no expenditure record to assign to any program of record.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: What do GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a, and the underlying SUPSHIP acceptance and inspection records they cite, establish about ship acceptance documentation and SUPSHIP's role in certifying completed work for CVN-79?
rows.target_document: SUPSHIP Newport News; GAO report source files
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the dossier's own document-control/accession register and the GAO engagement source-file request log for engagement codes corresponding to GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a; list every CVN-79 acceptance or inspection record series requested from SUPSHIP Newport News, with request date, release determination, and whether the item was delivered or withheld. Period: date of first GAO citation through current reconciliation cutoff.
rows.target_document: Dossier accession/document-control register and GAO source-file request log
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News (records custodian) and GAO engagement team of record
rows.period: 2018 through current reconciliation cutoff
rows.account: N/A - documentary holdings, no account
rows.hypothesis: The gap is a pure access/holdings question, not an analytic one: the GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a source files cited are GAO working-paper holdings (not the published reports), and the SUPSHIP acceptance and inspection records were never in the dossier's possession at all, so nothing about CVN-79 acceptance documentation was 'established' by them in this reconciliation. Cheapest kill: confirm whether the underlying record series was ever received.

rows.instruction: Trace the citation chain: pull the footnotes/endnotes in GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a that support the acceptance-documentation statements and identify by title and originating office each underlying record (INSURV trial report, acceptance instrument, SUPSHIP inspection report, material-inspection and receiving report). Record which office signed the acceptance determination for CVN-79 and which merely certified or witnessed work completion.
rows.target_document: GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a footnote/citation apparatus and the named underlying records
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News; Board of Inspection and Survey; NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: Report publication dates of GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a
rows.account: CVN-79 delivery/acceptance documentation
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label 'SUPSHIP acceptance and inspection records' is wrong or imprecise: the acceptance determination for CVN-79 rests with Board of Inspection and Survey (INSURV) trial reports and the Navy's formal acceptance/DD-250 or delivery-acceptance instrument, with SUPSHIP acting as on-site contractual authority rather than the certifying acceptance body. The label arrived with the question, not from a tested source.

rows.instruction: Read GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a for every acceptance-related finding and tag each by hull (CVN-78, CVN-79, class). Cross-check against the Ford-class SAR/APB for the same reporting years to confirm whether acceptance or completion status is reported at class level only. Period: SARs covering the GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a reporting years.
rows.target_document: GAO-2018a; GAO-2022a; Ford-class Selected Acquisition Report and single Ford-class APB
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 (Ford-class program office)
rows.period: Reporting years underlying GAO-2018a and GAO-2022a
rows.account: Ford-class APB / class-level acceptance and performance reporting
rows.hypothesis: The two GAO reports do not speak to CVN-79 hull-level acceptance at all: the cited findings about accepting incomplete ships are drawn from the lead ship CVN-78 and from class-level reporting, and were carried forward to CVN-79 by inference. Under class-level reporting conventions a class report cannot be assumed to yield a CVN-79 hull-level statement.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the CVN-79 delivery-strategy documentation: the contract modification(s) establishing and later rescinding the two-phase delivery plan, and the associated SUPSHIP Newport News work-completion certifications and inspection sign-offs for phase one versus final delivery. Compare against the FY24 President's Budget justification narrative attributing added funding to the longer schedule and new systems, and against the program-office statement that the strategy change created no new costs.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract modifications on delivery phasing; SUPSHIP phase-one and final completion certifications; FY24 SCN budget justification for CVN-79
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News; NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: Adoption of two-phase plan through FY24 budget submission
rows.account: SCN - CVN-79 detail design and construction; post-delivery accounts
rows.hypothesis: Acceptance documentation for CVN-79 is bifurcated by the former two-phase delivery plan: the records in existence certify preliminary acceptance at the end of phase one rather than a complete and deployable ship, so no single SUPSHIP certification marks 'work complete' and the delivery-versus-post-delivery boundary the reconciliation needs is not documented as a single event.

rows.instruction: Pull from SUPSHIP Newport News the CVN-79 contract administration file: progress-payment approvals, material inspection and receiving reports, and final-invoice/target-cost settlement correspondence, and identify the date and document by which completed work was certified for payment. Period: construction start through reconciliation cutoff.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract administration file (progress payments, MIRRs, invoice/settlement correspondence)
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News contracting office; DCMA/DFAS payment records
rows.period: CVN-79 construction start through reconciliation cutoff
rows.account: SCN - CVN-79 DD&C, fixed-price-incentive firm-target contract line items
rows.hypothesis: The acceptance boundary is defined by contract-type incentive structure rather than by inspection records: because CVN-79 DD&C is fixed-price-incentive firm-target, work-completion certification and the associated cost allocation flow through SUPSHIP's contractual/business authority (invoice, progress-payment and target-cost administration) rather than through acceptance inspection findings.

rows.instruction: Obtain the FY20 NDAA conference/mark language on CVN-79 acceptance and any implementing Navy guidance, then request from the F-35 Joint Program Office and from the SSDS and CEC program offices their CVN-79 installation and certification-of-capability records. Determine which office issues the certification that satisfies the acceptance condition and whether SUPSHIP certifications reference it.
rows.target_document: FY20 NDAA mark/conference language on CVN-79 acceptance; implementing Navy guidance; F-35C, SSDS and CEC installation/certification records for CVN-79
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News; F-35 Joint Program Office; SSDS and CEC program offices; NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: FY20 NDAA enactment through CVN-79 delivery
rows.account: CVN-79 acceptance conditions; separate programs of record (F-35C, SSDS, CEC) integration accounts
rows.hypothesis: Acceptance for CVN-79 was constrained by externally driven capability requirements (statutory language conditioning acceptance on F-35C capability, and systems that are separate programs of record), so completion certification depends on records held outside SUPSHIP and outside the carrier program, which is why the acceptance documentation question cannot be closed from SUPSHIP files alone.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Do separate acquisition program baselines, MDAP increment baselines, or sub-program baselines exist for the CVN-79 capabilities managed under the Ford-class program, and if so which office holds them?
rows.target_document: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) acquisition program baseline records / ASN(RDA) baseline repository
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from ASN(RDA) the baseline repository index entry for the Ford-class (CVN 78 class) program and pull the cover page, approval signature page, and schedule/cost/performance parameter tables of the currently approved APB and all prior approved revisions; confirm whether the document identifies a single program or enumerates ship-specific baselines, and whether CVN-79 appears as a separate baselined entity or only as a quantity/follow-on ship under the class parameters.
rows.target_document: Approved Ford-class acquisition program baseline and revision history
rows.target_system: ASN(RDA) APB repository / DoD Acquisition Visibility Environment
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) baseline repository (DAVE/DAES baseline record)
rows.period: Original APB approval through most recent approved revision
rows.account: SCN, Ford-class CVN 78 program (CVN-79 line)
rows.hypothesis: No CVN-79-specific acquisition program baseline exists; the Ford class is managed under a single class-level APB in which CVN-78 performance thresholds are applied to follow-on ships, so the only authoritative baseline available to reconcile against is class-level.

rows.instruction: Send a records-custody inquiry to PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) business financial management requesting identification of the office of record for the approved APB and any ship-level baseline documents, and separately ask ASN(RDA) acquisition management to state which office signed and retains the approved baseline; compare the two custody statements against the MDA designation in the program's approved acquisition strategy. Identify which source originally asserted PMS 378 custody in the dossier.
rows.target_document: Records-custody response and approved acquisition strategy MDA designation page
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) / ASN(RDA)
rows.period: Current
rows.account: Ford-class program baseline documentation (non-financial)
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label in the gap — that PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) holds CVN-79 baseline records — is an attribution that arrived with the question and may be wrong; baseline custody may rest with ASN(RDA) as MDA/approval authority while PMS 378 holds only derived program-management or contract-level cost products, not an APB.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the originating GAO or analytic report section that proposed separate APBs and cost baselines for future ship increments, together with the Navy/DoD written comments appended to that report and any DoD response-to-recommendation closure record; determine whether the recommendation was concurred with and implemented by establishment of a ship-level baseline, or closed without action.
rows.target_document: GAO report recommendation section plus agency comments and recommendation-status/closure record
rows.target_office: GAO recommendation follow-up file / OSD(A&S) recommendation response file
rows.period: From report publication through latest recommendation status update
rows.hypothesis: A separate CVN-79 baseline exists only as a proposal or recommendation in the source material (separate APBs, cost-estimation requirements, and cost baselines for future increments), and the dossier has mistaken a recommendation for an existing record.

rows.instruction: Pull the program's Selected Acquisition Report series and the DAES/DAVE program structure record for the Ford-class program and inspect the program-structure and subprogram designation fields for any declared increment, sub-program, block upgrade, or spiral tied to CVN-79; where a designation appears, request the corresponding subprogram baseline approval memorandum from ASN(RDA).
rows.target_document: Selected Acquisition Report program structure/subprogram sections and DAES program record
rows.target_system: DAVE / Defense Acquisition Management Information Retrieval successor system
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) / OUSD(A&S) acquisition information repository
rows.period: Milestone B through most recent annual SAR
rows.account: Ford-class MDAP program structure record
rows.hypothesis: CVN-79 capabilities are managed as an MDAP increment, sub-program, or block upgrade, which would require its own baseline and ship-specific naming, reporting, and scope treatment under MTA/subprogram guidance.

rows.instruction: Request from ASN(RDA) and PMS 378 the acquisition decision memoranda and program-structure determination correspondence addressing incorporation of F-35C capability and other newly added CVN-79 systems, and the FY24 budget justification exhibit narrative cited for the additional-funding request; determine whether any ADM establishes a separate managed program with its own baseline or folds the capability into the existing class baseline.
rows.target_document: Acquisition decision memoranda and FY24 SCN budget justification exhibit narrative
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) / PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378)
rows.period: FY20 NDAA cycle through FY24 budget submission
rows.account: SCN CVN-79 line, FY24 request for additional funding
rows.hypothesis: New or modified CVN-79 capabilities (e.g., F-35C integration, newly incorporated systems) were required under Navy instruction to be managed either separately or within the original program, so a decision record exists designating the management construct — and that record, not an APB, is where CVN-79 baseline status is fixed.

rows.instruction: Obtain the approved Ford-class acquisition strategy tailoring section specifying review and decision points, plus the CAPE/Navy independent cost estimate and service cost position inventory for the program; then request from SUPSHIP Newport News and PMS 378 the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract target-cost documentation and contract performance reports to establish whether hull-level figures are contract baselines rather than APB baselines.
rows.target_document: Approved acquisition strategy tailoring section; ICE/service cost position inventory; CVN-79 contract performance reports
rows.target_system: Earned value management central repository (CPR/IPMR submissions)
rows.target_office: PMS 378 business financial management / SUPSHIP Newport News / Navy Center for Cost Analysis
rows.period: Milestone C through current reporting period
rows.account: CVN-79 detail design and construction contract (FPI firm target) and construction-preparation modification
rows.hypothesis: Tailored shipbuilding milestone structure (combined Milestones B/C and post-Milestone C absence of milestone-driven independent cost estimates) means no ship-level cost baseline was ever generated for CVN-79, and any hull-level figures in circulation derive from contract or earned-value products rather than an approved baseline.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: What do the governing acquisition and reporting authorities for this program require as to ship-level versus class-level reporting and baseline scope, specifically SECNAVINST 5000.02G, the FY2013 National Defense Authorization Act provisions cited in the MSAR, 10 USC 8671, and APB Change 5's treatment of disposal costs within the O&S objective?
rows.target_document: ASN(RDA)/Navy acquisition policy office and the CVN-78 program office APB/statutory reference file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the verbatim reporting-requirement text of SECNAVINST 5000.02G (enclosure governing shipbuilding program reporting and baselines) and the signed APB Change 5 cover/approval page plus its performance-and-cost paragraphs from the CVN-78 program office APB/statutory reference file; read for any clause naming an individual hull as a reporting unit. One reading of two documents kills or confirms the premise.
rows.target_document: SECNAVINST 5000.02G and CVN-78 Class APB Change 5 (signed, with change pages)
rows.target_office: CVN-78 (Ford class) program office APB/statutory reference file (PEO Aircraft Carriers)
rows.period: APB Change 5 approval date through current MSAR reporting year
rows.account: CVN-78 Class APB / acquisition reporting requirements
rows.hypothesis: The question's premise that these four authorities (SECNAVINST 5000.02G, the FY2013 NDAA provisions, 10 USC 8671, APB Change 5) impose a hull-level reporting requirement for CVN-79 is an inherited label; the governing instruction and single Ford-class APB may require only class/subprogram-level reporting, in which case no CVN-79 hull-level figure is required to exist and the reconciliation boundary must be drawn at class level.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the statutory-authority / legislative-reference section of the current CVN-78 Class MSAR and transcribe the exact public-law section numbers cited, then pull those sections as codified and as amended from the program office statutory reference file; compare to the question's 'FY2013 NDAA' label and to the congressional notification package that raised the CVN-79 Cost Limitation Baseline.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR statutory-authority section plus cited public-law text and the CVN-79 cost-cap congressional notification letter
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) Navy acquisition policy office; CVN-78 program office statutory reference file
rows.period: FY2013 enactment through most recent congressional notification and the current MSAR reporting year
rows.account: CVN-79 Cost Limitation Baseline and full-funding authority
rows.hypothesis: The MSAR's citation of 'FY2013 NDAA provisions' is itself an unverified attribution carried into the question; the provisions actually cited in the MSAR statutory-authority block may be the cost-limitation and full-funding sections as later amended rather than as originally enacted, so the cap and full-funding scope differ from what the question assumes.

rows.instruction: Pull the current codified text and notes of 10 USC 8671 (including its editorial renumbering history from the prior title-10 section) from the ASN(RDA) acquisition policy office legal reference set, and check against the MSAR's own citation of it for the reporting year in question.
rows.target_document: 10 USC 8671 codified text with source and amendment notes
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) Navy acquisition policy office (counsel reference set)
rows.period: Current codification, with renumbering history
rows.account: Statutory cost limitation / full funding authority
rows.hypothesis: 10 USC 8671's subject matter may not be the carrier cost-limitation authority the question treats it as; the section's actual scope (and whether it addresses hull-level accounting at all) must be read before it is allowed to bound the reconciliation.

rows.instruction: Read the O&S cost section of signed APB Change 5 (objective/threshold table and its definitional footnotes) side by side with the MSAR O&S section's methodology note on average annual cost per ship, ship count and service life, and with the program-manager approval memo for the current O&S and disposal estimates; look specifically for whether inactivation/disposal is named as in-scope to the O&S objective.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class APB Change 5, O&S cost section and footnotes; current CVN-78 Class MSAR O&S section; PM approval memo for O&S/disposal estimates
rows.target_office: CVN-78 program office cost estimating / APB file
rows.period: APB Change 5 approval date and the current MSAR O&S estimate vintage
rows.account: O&S objective and inactivation/disposal cost estimate
rows.hypothesis: APB Change 5 places disposal inside the O&S objective (rather than outside it), because the MSAR's O&S construction runs through service life including inactivation and folds EMALS inactivation and disposal into class inactivation-and-disposal cost; if so the reconciliation may count disposal, and conversely a Change 5 O&S definition silent on disposal would exclude it.

rows.instruction: Obtain the ASN(RDA)-approved acquisition strategy / tailoring memorandum and Acquisition Decision Memoranda for the CVN-78 Class covering CVN-79, and read the paragraphs specifying review and decision-point timing and the statutory reporting carve-outs; confirm whether any per-hull reporting or decision point is designated.
rows.target_document: ASN(RDA) acquisition strategy approval and tailoring memo, plus CVN-78 Class ADMs
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) acquisition policy office; PEO Aircraft Carriers program file
rows.period: From the CVN-79 acquisition strategy approval through the latest ADM
rows.account: Program structure / milestone tailoring and reporting obligations
rows.hypothesis: The absence of required hull-level figures is explained by a tailored shipbuilding milestone structure (combined MS B/C and combined development/initial-production commitments) under SECNAVINST 5000.02G, where the tailoring document defines reviews and decision points at the class level while still having to satisfy statutory reporting and sustainment requirements; the tailoring memo, not the instruction's base text, sets what must be reported per hull.

rows.instruction: Lay the APB Change 5 cost table, the MSAR acquisition-cost table (appropriations vs expenditures, quantity basis, EMALS subprogram exclusion) and the PB 2027 SCN budget exhibit for line 2001 against each other and record for each the dollar basis, quantity basis and shared/sunk labeling as printed in the column headings; flag any authority-required figure that has no like-basis counterpart.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class APB Change 5 cost table; CVN-78 Class MSAR acquisition cost and funding sections; PB 2027 SCN budget justification exhibit
rows.target_office: CVN-78 program office business financial manager; Navy budget office (FMB)
rows.period: Base-year 2000 columns through the PB 2027 current estimate
rows.account: CVN-78 subprogram acquisition cost, procurement line 2001
rows.hypothesis: Even if an authority requires a hull-level or baseline-scope figure, the retrievable figures are not comparable across the authorities because APB, MSAR and budget-exhibit scope and dollar bases differ (base-year vs then-year vs report-fiscal-year; six-carrier quantity; shared and sunk line labels), so the apparent reporting-requirement gap is a scope/basis mismatch rather than a missing requirement.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the FY2001 and FY2025 DOT&E annual reports, CVN 78 TEMP Revision F, and Enterprise TEMP 1910 be obtained to determine the coordinated test scope and which test activities are funded inside the CVN-79 construction effort versus by separate programs of record?
rows.target_document: DOT&E and the CVN-78 program office test and evaluation master plan library
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the DoD TEMP registry / DOT&E Oversight List document index for the string "1910" and for "Enterprise" as a ship name, and separately ask the CVN-78 Class Program Office (PMS 378) T&E lead to identify by hull (CVN 65, CVN 78, CVN 80) which TEMP bears number 1910 and its approval date. Record which source originally asserted the "Enterprise TEMP 1910" label in the gap text — the gap question itself, not a Navy document, is the only present attestation.
rows.target_document: Enterprise TEMP 1910 (identifier as asserted in GAP PQ-21555673)
rows.target_system: DoD TEMP registry / DOT&E document index
rows.target_office: PMS 378 Test and Evaluation lead; DOT&E Oversight List staff
rows.period: Document-identification check, current holdings as of latest TEMP revision
rows.account: T&E documentation identifiers; no financial account
rows.hypothesis: The named executor label is wrong in part: "Enterprise TEMP 1910" is an inherited document identifier that arrived with the question and may not be a DOT&E/CVN-78 program-office TEMP at all (it may be a legacy CVN 65 Enterprise document, a TEMP registration number, or a mislabeled CVN 80 Enterprise (CVN-80) TEMP). If the identifier resolves to the wrong hull, the whole retrieval task is misdirected and no coordinated test scope can be derived from it.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-78 Class MSAR (latest, PB 2027 cycle) funding tables and read the per-line program attribution for SSDS and CEC-related procurement and RDT&E lines, specifically checking procurement line 2001 and every line carrying the "Shared" marker, against the separate SSDS and CEC program-of-record MSARs/budget exhibits for the same period. If SSDS/CEC appear only in their own program ledgers, the TEMP retrieval is moot.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR; SSDS and CEC program MSARs
rows.target_system: DAVE / Defense Acquisition Visibility Environment MSAR repository
rows.target_office: PMS 378 cost/business financial manager; PEO IWS for SSDS/CEC
rows.period: PB 2027 current estimate column
rows.account: CVN-78 Class MSAR procurement line 2001 and Shared-marked lines; SSDS and CEC program-of-record procurement lines
rows.hypothesis: The retrieval is unnecessary for the stated blocker because the SSDS and CEC test activity costs are already excluded from the CVN-79 hull ledger by virtue of those systems being separate programs of record with their own funding lines — the TEMPs would document test coordination, not funding attribution. The gap could be closed from MSAR/SAR line attribution alone without any TEMP.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the FY2001 and FY2025 DOT&E Annual Report to Congress from the DOT&E public report archive and locate the CVN 78 / CVX / SSDS / CEC program write-ups; confirm classification markings and distribution statement on each write-up. Note separately whether the FY2025 report's CVN 78 entry cross-references a TEMP revision letter.
rows.target_document: DOT&E Annual Report to Congress, FY2001 and FY2025
rows.target_office: DOT&E Director's reports staff
rows.period: FY2001 and FY2025 annual report editions
rows.account: None — T&E reporting document
rows.hypothesis: The FY2001 DOT&E annual report is a published, releasable document and is already in the open record; only the TEMPs carry an access restriction. The "access_required" closability tag may therefore be over-applied to the whole bundle, making part of the retrieval free.

rows.instruction: Ask PMS 378's T&E and Evaluation Master Plan librarian for the full revision history of the CVN 78 TEMP — approval dates, revision letters, and whether a CVN-78 Class TEMP supersedes hull-specific revisions — and obtain the approval memo for whichever revision is current. Compare the revision letter in the gap text against that history.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 TEMP, all revisions (asserted Revision F)
rows.target_system: PMS 378 T&E document library / NAVSEA records
rows.target_office: CVN-78 program office TEMP library (PMS 378)
rows.period: All CVN 78 TEMP revisions through current
rows.account: None — T&E documentation
rows.hypothesis: TEMP Revision F may be superseded or may not exist under that revision letter; the gap may be chasing a revision that was never approved (CVN-78 TEMPs are frequently re-lettered or rolled into a class TEMP). The cited revision letter is an inherited label from the question text.
