rows.instruction: Obtain the CVN-79 Acquisition Strategy and the contract modification documentation that moved work from post-shakedown availability into construction, plus the modification that effected the two-phase to single-phase delivery change, from the NAVSEA 02 contracting file for the CVN-79 detail-design-and-construction contract; read the scope statements for warfare-systems test and activation work and the preliminary-turnover vs final-delivery milestone definitions.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 Acquisition Strategy; CVN-79 DD&C contract modifications (single-phase conversion; PSA-to-construction transfer)
rows.target_system: Electronic Document Access (EDA) / NAVSEA contract file
rows.target_office: NAVSEA 02 / SUPSHIP Newport News contracting officer; PMS 378
rows.period: Original award through latest modification
rows.account: CVN-79 detail design and construction contract scope; post-shakedown availability work transferred to construction
rows.hypothesis: Even if all four documents are obtained, they will not resolve the funding-attribution question because the test scope is partitioned by the acquisition strategy's phase construct rather than by TEMP, and CVN-79 has since shifted from two-phase to single-phase delivery with complete warfare systems delivered inside the current construction period. The delivery-phase assumption, not the TEMP, controls which test activity sits in the hull total.

rows.instruction: Request from DCARC the CSDR compliance assessment for the CVN-78 subprogram (not the program roll-up) and the submission inventory for the CVN-79 DD&C contract, identifying which WBS elements covering test and activation have accepted versus delinquent or waived submissions for the current reporting period.
rows.target_document: DCARC CSDR compliance assessment, CVN-78 subprogram
rows.target_office: Defense Cost and Resource Center (DCARC)
rows.period: Current CSDR reporting period and prior submissions of record
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C CSDR submissions; test and activation WBS elements
rows.hypothesis: Any test-activity cost pulled from CSDR to corroborate the TEMP scope will be unreliable at the CVN-78 subprogram level, so the retrieval would produce an unverifiable answer even if granted; the subprogram's CSDR compliance is rated Red while the program-level rating is Green, and conflating the two would make a CSDR pull look complete when it is not.

rows.instruction: query: Which appropriation accounts and program records document the Ford-class development work that was directed into shipbuilding accounts rather than RDT&E, and how is that content identified within CVN-79 shipbuilding records?
rows.target_system: NAVSEA FMB / PMS 378 budget execution records for SCN line 1611N and the RDT&E-to-SCN strategy change file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN 78 Class MSAR (latest, PB 2027 current-estimate column plus the base-year-2000 column) acquisition-estimate table and read the appropriation-account rows for SCN 1611N; record every account code and row label shown and whether any row is captioned as development, non-recurring engineering or class design. One-table read, no system access needed.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR acquisition-estimate-by-appropriation table
rows.period: PB 2027 current estimate and BY2000 baseline columns
rows.account: SCN 1611N
rows.hypothesis: The "development directed into shipbuilding accounts" content is identified in the MSAR's own account-by-account acquisition estimate structure, i.e. it is already visible as the 1611N shipbuilding account line of the CVN 78 subprogram and is not a hidden embedded item at all. Killing or confirming this requires only reading the subprogram's appropriation-account breakout for the account labels and any development/non-recurring-engineering annotations attached to 1611N.

rows.instruction: In the same MSAR, list the full set of acquisition-estimate accounts for the CVN 78 subprogram (shipbuilding line, Other Procurement Navy line, and the named CVN-79 ship-integration RDT&E project line) and confirm against the gap record whether any residual is carried as unexplained. Desk check against the dossier's own exposure field.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR; GAP PQ-ac29b248 exposure field
rows.period: current MSAR reporting year
rows.account: SCN 1611N; OPN; CVN-79 ship-integration RDT&E project
rows.hypothesis: The gap is answerable at zero cost because the exposure is recorded as nothing left unexplained: the question is a scope/identification question, not a dollar-reconciliation question, and the accounts sought are simply the set already enumerated in the subprogram estimate (shipbuilding, Other Procurement Navy, plus the CVN-79-specific ship-integration RDT&E project). Cheapest kill: check whether any dollar quantity is actually unexplained before any retrieval is tasked.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the named RDT&E-to-SCN strategy change file held by PMS 378 (the source that asserts the CVN 21 strategy change) and read the directive language verbatim for which accounts it names and whether any later decision memorandum amends it; cross-check against the MSAR's continued listing of a CVN-79 ship-integration RDT&E project, which would contradict a total migration out of R&D.
rows.target_document: RDT&E-to-SCN strategy change file
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378
rows.period: CVN 21 program-initiation era through current MSAR
rows.account: RDT&E and SCN
rows.hypothesis: INHERITED LABEL: the premise that an "early CVN 21 strategy change directed development and ship purchases to shipbuilding accounts rather than R&D" is an attribution that arrived with the question and may be a paraphrase of a strategy document that in fact split development across both account families, or that was superseded. The label, not the money, should be tested first.

rows.instruction: In the MSAR funding tables, extract every line carrying a Shared or Sunk flag, including procurement line 2001, and record the flag definitions and footnotes; determine whether any class-development content sits under those flags rather than under a CVN-79-identified row.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR funding tables with Shared/Sunk flags
rows.period: budget year and remaining FYDP
rows.account: SCN 1611N; procurement line 2001
rows.hypothesis: The content is not identifiable as a CVN-79 hull item at all because the relevant rows are subprogram-level or explicitly flagged Shared or Sunk, so class development residing in shipbuilding accounts cannot be attributed to CVN-79 construction without a split; the apparent double-counting risk is a labeling artifact of Shared/Sunk/shared-procurement lines.

rows.instruction: Request from NAVSEA FMB / PMS 378 the CVN-79 construction-preparation award and the detail-design-and-construction award (full contract numbers, not trailing digits, to avoid mixing CVN-80) and pull the corresponding DCARC CSDR submissions with their compliance assessment; read the WBS for design/non-recurring-engineering elements funded from SCN. Note the Red subprogram CSDR rating means the pull must not be assumed complete.
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 / FMB
rows.period: CVN-79 ConPrep award through latest CSDR submission
rows.account: SCN 1611N via CVN-79 ConPrep and DD&C contracts
rows.hypothesis: Class development content inside shipbuilding figures is identifiable only through contract-level and CSDR work-breakdown records (construction preparation, detail design and construction as distinct awards), not through appropriation tables; the identification mechanism is the DD&C/ConPrep award structure and WBS elements for design and non-recurring engineering.

rows.instruction: Pull the PMS 378 contract modification file for CVN-79 covering the PSA-to-construction work transfer, the single-phase delivery decision document, and the modification incorporating AAG and jet-blast-deflector changes; map each modification's scope statement against the SCN 1611N execution rows for the same fiscal years in NAVSEA FMB budget execution records.
rows.target_office: NAVSEA PMS 378 contracts file / NAVSEA FMB budget execution
rows.period: from CVN-79 DD&C award through the latest modification
rows.account: SCN 1611N
rows.hypothesis: Any apparent unexplained content in CVN-79 shipbuilding records is scope migration rather than misplaced development funding: work moved out of post-shakedown availability into construction, the shift from two-phase to single-phase delivery, and later capability/safety modifications all enlarge the construction account without being class development.

rows.instruction: query: Which outside-program records (for technologies developed by programs other than the carrier program) carry CVN-79-related content, and how, if at all, are those costs reflected in or excluded from CVN-79 program records?
rows.target_system: PMS 378 government-furnished-equipment cost sponsor list and the responsible other-program offices
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the AAG program annual MSAR procurement funding exhibit and the CVN-78 Class MSAR procurement exhibit for the same reporting period (latest MSAR cycle plus the prior cycle), and compare line-by-line against the AAG lines carried in the CVN-79 appropriation/expenditure tables; confirm with the AAG program office whether its reported procurement lines are the same obligations shown in the carrier class report.
rows.target_document: AAG annual MSAR and CVN-78 Class MSAR procurement funding exhibits
rows.target_office: AAG program office and PMS 378 MSAR preparer
rows.period: Latest two MSAR reporting cycles
rows.account: AAG procurement (SCN/OPN as reported) for CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The outside-program CVN-79 content is concentrated in AAG, which is a separate program of record whose procurement funding is reported in both the AAG program's own annual MSAR and the CVN-78 Class MSAR, so the apparent outside-program amount is already present in CVN-79/class records and adding the two reports would double count rather than reveal excluded capability.

rows.instruction: Request from the SSDS and CEC program offices their procurement and RDT&E budget justification exhibits (P-forms and R-2/R-2A) for the fiscal years spanning CVN-79 combat-system installation and light-off, and extract every line whose remarks or ship-set narrative names CVN-79; then check whether those same lines appear anywhere in the PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor list.
rows.target_document: SSDS and CEC program budget justification exhibits
rows.target_office: SSDS program office, CEC program office, PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor list
rows.period: FYs covering CVN-79 combat system installation and test
rows.account: SSDS and CEC procurement and RDT&E lines naming CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: The outside-program records are the SSDS and CEC program-of-record submissions, which carry CVN-79 installation/testing content in their own budget exhibits and are excluded from the CVN-79 hull ledger because the carrier program reports them only as government-furnished equipment coordination, not as hull cost.

rows.instruction: For each item on the PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor list, retrieve the sponsoring appropriation, line/sub-line and program element from the cost sponsor list itself and trace that program element in the Navy budget exhibits for the same fiscal years; flag any item whose program element resolves back to a carrier-program line (including the CVN-79 ship-integration RDT&E project) and ask the PMS 378 preparer which source originally asserted the outside-program attribution.
rows.target_document: PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor list with sponsoring program elements; Navy budget exhibits for the cited PEs
rows.target_office: PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor manager
rows.period: Current MSAR reporting year and preceding FYDP
rows.account: Program elements cited on the PMS 378 GFE cost sponsor list
rows.hypothesis: The inherited framing that these are "outside-program" costs is a label from the MSAR/GAO technology-maturity discussion rather than a funding fact: the named items may be funded inside the carrier program's own lines (as nuclear costs are, residing within the Navy funding line rather than a separate resource line), so there is no outside-program ledger to reconcile for part of the list.

rows.instruction: Obtain the backup worksheets behind the MSAR funding table for procurement line 2001 and every other line flagged Shared or Sunk, and ask the PMS 378 MSAR preparer for the allocation basis identifying which non-CVN-79 activities and which outside programs those lines fund in the budget year and remaining FYDP.
rows.target_document: MSAR funding exhibit backup worksheets and allocation basis memo
rows.target_office: PMS 378 MSAR preparer
rows.period: Budget year plus remaining FYDP of the current MSAR
rows.account: MSAR procurement line 2001 and all Shared/Sunk-flagged lines
rows.hypothesis: Lines in the CVN-79 records marked "Shared" or "Sunk" are the mechanism by which outside-program and other-ship content is already folded into carrier records, so the supposed exclusion is a labeling artifact: shared lines include non-CVN-79 activity and sunk lines conceal historical outside-program spending.

rows.instruction: Retrieve the General Atomics EMALS/AAG shipset contract file from the awarding contracting office, including the CLIN structure, the CVN-80 option exercise modifications, and any hull allocation or ship-set delivery schedule; compare against the EMALS subprogram columns in the CVN-78 Class MSAR acquisition estimate to determine whether a CVN-79-only split exists in the record.
rows.target_document: EMALS/AAG shipset contract file and CVN-78 Class MSAR EMALS subprogram exhibit
rows.target_office: NAVSEA contracting office of record for the EMALS shipset contract; General Atomics contract administration via PCO
rows.period: Award date through latest modification
rows.account: EMALS and AAG shipset contract CLINs and EMALS subprogram acquisition estimate
rows.hypothesis: EMALS, reported as a distinct subprogram with its own contracts and no comparable antecedent, is the record boundary that moves CVN-79 content in and out of the hull ledger: shipset and option structures covering CVN-79 together with CVN-80 mean portions of the outside-program content are reported at subprogram or multi-ship level and cannot be assigned to the CVN-79 hull without a split.

rows.instruction: Request from the PMS 378 contracts office the CVN-79 contract modification file for the post-shakedown-availability-to-construction transfer and the single-phase delivery restructure, with the associated scope crosswalk identifying which GFE-furnished systems moved, and reconcile that crosswalk against the preliminary-turnover versus final-delivery work lists; separately ask the responsible other-program offices whether any CVN-79-labeled item in their records was later backfit or forward-fit to another hull.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract modification files with scope crosswalk; preliminary turnover and final delivery work lists
rows.target_office: PMS 378 contracts office and the responsible other-program offices
rows.period: Date of two-phase-to-single-phase restructure through current reporting
rows.account: CVN-79 construction and post-shakedown availability work scope, GFE-furnished systems
rows.hypothesis: Part of the outside-program content is not excluded but relocated across hulls and phases: technologies developed for one ship were fitted to later ships or backfit to earlier ones, and the single-phase delivery shift plus the modification moving post-shakedown work into construction changed which outside-program-furnished work sits in the CVN-79 construction ledger versus a later hull's or a later availability's record.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the GAO (2017b) report cited for the independent-estimate and milestone history be obtained to verify when independent cost estimates were prepared for individual carriers and which milestone decisions they supported?
rows.target_document: GAO published reports / Navy CAPE and program office independent cost estimate file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the source dossier's own reference list entry for "GAO 2017b" and resolve it to a GAO product number via GAO.gov's published-reports index for calendar year 2017, restricted to Ford-class/CVN products; then confirm the resolved product's text actually contains the independent-cost-estimate and milestone-history passages attributed to it. Cheapest possible kill: if the reference list resolves to a product whose scope is class-level shipbuilding or ship delivery acceptance rather than independent cost estimates, the label is wrong and the gap is reframed, not closed.
rows.target_document: GAO 2017 Ford-class / CVN report resolved from dossier reference list
rows.target_office: GAO (published reports index)
rows.account: CVN-79 / Ford class (CVN 78 class) SCN
rows.hypothesis: The "GAO (2017b)" label is an inherited citation artifact: the report exists and is publicly retrievable, and the closability question is answered simply by resolving the citation string in the dossier's reference list to a GAO product number. The attribution arrived with the question, not from a verified bibliographic check, and may point to a different GAO product (e.g., an annual weapon systems assessment chapter rather than a carrier-specific report) than the independent-estimate/milestone content ascribed to it.

rows.instruction: In the resolved GAO 2017 product, read the cost-estimate and baseline sections and its appendix tables for any row keyed to CVN-79 as distinct from the Ford-class aggregate; also check the GAO highlights page and scope-and-methodology appendix for whether GAO stated it reviewed ship-specific versus program-level estimates. Kill cheaply: a scope statement limited to the program/APB level disconfirms hull-level content.
rows.target_document: Resolved GAO 2017 Ford-class report, cost/baseline sections and scope-and-methodology appendix
rows.target_office: GAO
rows.account: CVN-79 hull-level vs Ford-class program aggregate
rows.hypothesis: The report is obtainable but cannot answer the blocking question, because the cited GAO product reports at class level only and contains no CVN-79 hull-level independent estimate. Retrievability and informativeness are separate questions, and the gap is closable as DOCUMENT-obtained / question-unanswered.

rows.instruction: Request from OSD CAPE the index of independent cost estimates and independent cost assessments logged under the Ford-class (CVN 78 class) MDAP from the Milestone B/C decision forward, asking specifically whether any entry is scoped to CVN-79 rather than the class. Pair with the Ford-class Milestone C Acquisition Decision Memorandum to see whether any follow-on-ship decision point was scheduled that would trigger a new estimate. Kill cheaply: a CAPE index with no CVN-79-scoped entry and an ADM with no follow-on decision point disconfirms existence of the artifact.
rows.target_document: OSD CAPE independent cost estimate/assessment log; Ford-class Milestone C Acquisition Decision Memorandum
rows.target_office: OSD CAPE (Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation)
rows.period: Milestone C decision through present
rows.account: Ford class (CVN 78 class) MDAP
rows.hypothesis: No milestone-driven independent cost estimate was ever required or prepared for CVN-79 specifically, because single-MDAP management meant post-Milestone C follow-on hulls triggered no new independent-estimate requirement; the GAO report, however obtained, would document the absence rather than the artifact.

rows.instruction: Request from PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) the CVN-79 detail design and construction fixed-price-incentive contract award file, specifically the service cost position / program office estimate and any CAPE concurrence memo, plus the SUPSHIP Newport News cost and pricing documentation supporting the firm-target negotiation. Determine from the signature block whether the estimating organization was independent of the program office. Kill cheaply: absence of any CAPE concurrence memo in the award file disconfirms the "independent" label.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract award cost file: service cost position, program office estimate, CAPE concurrence memo
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers / PMS 378; SUPSHIP Newport News
rows.period: CVN-79 DD&C contract award and construction-preparation modification
rows.account: CVN-79 SCN detail design and construction
rows.hypothesis: A CVN-79 cost estimate exists but as a program-office or SUPSHIP service cost position tied to contract award rather than as an independent (CAPE) estimate; the question's "independent-estimate" label conflates the two, and the external comparison point sought for the reconciliation is actually a non-independent artifact.

rows.instruction: Compare the scope statement of any located CVN-79 estimate against the FY24 President's Budget SCN justification exhibit (Budget Item Justification sheet) for CVN-79, reading the narrative attributing additional funding to schedule length and new system incorporation; also obtain the program office position provided to GAO asserting the delivery-strategy change created no new costs. Kill cheaply: if the budget exhibit narrative lists content absent from the estimate's scope, non-comparability is established without further retrieval.
rows.target_document: FY2024 President's Budget SCN budget item justification exhibit, CVN-79; program office response to GAO on delivery-strategy change
rows.target_office: Navy Office of Budget (FMB) / PMS 378
rows.period: FY2024 budget submission
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79
rows.hypothesis: Any CVN-79 estimate that exists is non-comparable as an external hull-level reconciliation point because the hull's scope changed after the estimate was prepared: delivery-strategy change, two-phase-to-single-delivery revision, F-35C integration, and new-system incorporation altered content without a restated baseline. Obtaining the GAO report would not yield a like-for-like comparison.

rows.instruction: Check the resolved GAO 2017 product's front matter for a statement that a classified or limited-official-use annex was issued separately, then query GAO's Congressional Relations office for the annex's distribution status; in parallel, request the Selected Acquisition Report and statutory milestone reporting submissions for the Ford class to see whether required reporting elements carry the estimate content. Kill cheaply: absence of an annex notice in the front matter disconfirms the restricted-annex path.
rows.target_document: Resolved GAO 2017 product front matter and any limited-distribution annex; Ford-class Selected Acquisition Report
rows.target_office: GAO Congressional Relations; OUSD(A&S) acquisition reporting
rows.period: CY2017 and surrounding SAR cycles
rows.account: Ford class (CVN 78 class) MDAP reporting
rows.hypothesis: Hull-level independent estimate content exists but resides in a restricted or non-public channel, so the document is unobtainable in the open version while remaining retrievable through a controlled request; the GAO product is the public abstract of a limited-distribution annex.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the Section 121(b) certification package and the CAPE independent two-ship savings estimate be obtained to compare their treatment of government-furnished equipment and production change orders?
rows.target_document: OSD CAPE and ASN(RDA) two-ship-buy certification file
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query the ASN(RDA) acquisition correspondence/records office for the two-ship-buy certification file index covering the CVN-80/CVN-81 certification transmittal period, requesting control number, classification/distribution caveat and release authority for the Section 121(b) certification package; simultaneously query OSD CAPE records for the independent two-ship savings estimate backup file for the same certification period. Ask only for existence, custodian and release status.
rows.target_document: Section 121(b) certification package transmittal and CAPE independent two-ship savings estimate
rows.target_system: ASN(RDA) acquisition records index / CAPE ICE file index
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) and OSD CAPE
rows.period: Certification transmittal year through next full budget submission
rows.account: CVN-80/CVN-81 two-ship buy certification record
rows.hypothesis: The documents exist but are access-controlled rather than absent: the Section 121(b) certification package is held as a controlled-distribution file by ASN(RDA) and the CAPE two-ship savings estimate as a CAPE ICE-support working file, so closure requires a release/need-to-know determination, not a search. Cheapest to kill: a single records-status query returns either a control number or a 'no such record' answer.

rows.instruction: Trace the label to its asserting source: pull the congressional notification and authorization-act citation used in the Navy's two-ship-buy certification letter to the defense committees for the certification year, and confirm which statutory subsection the certification was made under. Check the MSAR/SAR narrative section that describes the two-ship-buy authority for the same year, and record which document first asserts 'Section 121(b)'.
rows.target_document: Navy two-ship-buy certification letter to defense committees and the MSAR acquisition-strategy narrative
rows.target_office: ASN(RDA) legislative affairs / Navy OLA
rows.period: Certification year
rows.account: Two-ship-buy statutory authority citation
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label 'Section 121(b)' may misname the authority actually invoked for the two-ship buy certification, in which case the named file does not exist under that citation and retrieval keyed to it will always fail. The label arrived with the question rather than from a cited document.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-78 Class MSAR sections on acquisition strategy and cost-estimate comparison for the certification year and the following year, and the GAO shipbuilding/annual-weapons-assessment chapter covering the CVN-80/CVN-81 two-ship buy, searching for named GFE and production-change-order assumption differences between the Navy and CAPE savings estimates.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR acquisition-strategy and cost sections; GAO review of the two-ship buy
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers (PMS 378) cost lead
rows.period: Certification year and following budget year
rows.account: CVN-80/CVN-81 two-ship savings estimate assumptions
rows.hypothesis: The GFE and production-change-order treatment difference is already documented in a derivative product (MSAR narrative, GAO or CRS review of the two-ship buy) that quotes both estimates' assumptions, so the comparison can be closed without obtaining either primary file.

rows.instruction: Request from PEO Aircraft Carriers the hull-allocation methodology memo (or contract line item structure) for the CVN-80/CVN-81 DD&C modification and for the shared GFE purchase lines, covering the certification year forward, and check whether the MSAR procurement lines marked 'Shared' for the same year carry a stated CVN-79 allocation rule.
rows.target_document: Hull-allocation methodology memo and contract line item structure for the combined DD&C modification
rows.target_office: PEO Aircraft Carriers / PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: Certification year through current budget year
rows.account: Shared GFE purchase lines and CVN-80/CVN-81 DD&C modification
rows.hypothesis: Even if both files are obtained, they will not resolve the CVN-79 attribution because the GFE savings and production change orders are defined at the shared CVN-80/CVN-81 award level and the single combined DD&C modification value cannot be split to a hull without a separate allocation basis, making the retrieval necessary but not sufficient.

rows.instruction: Pull the GFE/government-furnished-materiel breakout from the CVN-78 Class MSAR and the EMALS/AAG production-contract line structure for the certification year, and confirm whether the EMALS and AAG shipsets exercised as CVN-80 options under the CVN-79 shipset contract are carried as GFE in the Navy savings estimate, in the CAPE estimate, or in neither. Check the AAG program MSAR for overlap before combining.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR GFE breakout and EMALS/AAG production contract line structure
rows.target_office: PMS 378 and the EMALS/AAG program office
rows.period: Certification year and prior year
rows.account: GFE / GFM categories including EMALS and AAG shipsets
rows.hypothesis: The scope label 'government-furnished equipment' in the question may conflate distinct categories that the two estimates handle in separate places: launch-and-recovery shipsets procured under separate awards (EMALS/AAG) versus general GFE purchases shared with CVN-80, so a comparison keyed to a single GFE heading will not line up between the two estimates.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-79 DD&C contract modification register from the Navy contract file (PMS 378 / NAVSEA 02 contracting officer) for the period spanning the two-phase-to-single-phase change through the certification year, and identify for each modification which baseline it adjusts; then compare that register's baseline date against the baseline dates stated in the Navy and CAPE two-ship savings estimates.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 DD&C contract modification register and estimate baseline statements
rows.target_office: NAVSEA contracting officer / PMS 378
rows.period: Two-phase-to-single-phase change through certification year
rows.account: CVN-79 DD&C contract modifications and PSA-to-construction work transfers
rows.hypothesis: The production-change-order element of the comparison is not separable because CVN-79 contract modifications moved work between PSA and construction, shifted phase-II work into the single-phase delivery, and added capability/safety scope, so change orders in the certification-period baselines are measured against different baselines in the two estimates.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: What documentation establishes whether the EMALS subprogram acquisition, O&S and MILCON estimates are included within or additional to the CVN 78 subprogram estimates?
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR preparer (PMS 378 business financial manager) and the EMALS program office
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN 78 Class MSAR (most recent submission, PB 2027 cycle) and read the quantity-definition footnote and unit-of-measure line on the CVN-78 subprogram acquisition cost estimate page, together with the EMALS subprogram quantity page, as prepared by PMS 378's business financial manager. Record the verbatim exclusion/inclusion wording and whether it is scoped to acquisition only.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR (Major Subprogram Acquisition Report), quantity and cost-estimate sections
rows.target_office: PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: Current MSAR / PB 2027 submission
rows.account: Acquisition cost estimate, CVN-78 subprogram and EMALS subprogram
rows.hypothesis: The inclusion/exclusion relationship is stated on the face of the CVN-78 Class MSAR acquisition estimate itself: the subprogram quantity definition carries an explicit exclusion of the EMALS subprogram, which would establish EMALS acquisition estimates as additive rather than embedded.

rows.instruction: In the same CVN 78 Class MSAR, compare three sections side by side for scope statements: (a) the EMALS O&S cost-element estimate page, (b) the EMALS MILCON acquisition estimate page with its ASN FMB-6 conversion-source citation, and (c) the carrier-class inactivation-and-disposal estimate. Note for each whether an inclusion/exclusion statement exists at all; absence in O&S or MILCON kills the single-document hypothesis immediately.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR — EMALS subprogram O&S, MILCON and class disposal sections
rows.target_office: PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: Current MSAR / PB 2027 submission
rows.account: O&S cost elements; MILCON acquisition; inactivation and disposal
rows.hypothesis: The exclusion language is acquisition-only and does not travel to O&S or MILCON, so the three estimate types have different inclusion relationships and no single document resolves all three.

rows.instruction: Read the CVN 78 Class MSAR O&S section's methodology paragraph (average annual cost per ship x ship count x service life, including inactivation before decommissioning) and the adjacent disposal note, and confirm with the PMS 378 cost lead whether the per-ship average already embeds EMALS sustainment. One paragraph read; disconfirms or confirms without any cross-office tasking.
rows.target_document: CVN 78 Class MSAR, O&S methodology and disposal note
rows.target_office: PMS 378 business financial manager (cost lead)
rows.period: Current MSAR / PB 2027 submission
rows.account: O&S total and inactivation/disposal
rows.hypothesis: The disposal leg is already settled in the opposite direction from acquisition — EMALS inactivation and disposal are stated as rolled into the class figure — which means at least one of the three estimate types is inclusive and the dossier's framing of a uniform 'within or additional' answer is itself wrong.

rows.instruction: Request from the EMALS program office the scope-of-reporting statement for the EMALS production contract covering CVN-79 and CVN-80, and separately pull the AAG program's own annual MSAR procurement-funding section. Compare against the CVN 78 Class MSAR passage stating AAG procurement funding appears in both reports, and determine whether EMALS subprogram reporting is EMALS-only or EMALS-plus-AAG.
rows.target_document: EMALS production contract scope-of-reporting statement; AAG program annual MSAR
rows.target_office: EMALS program office; AAG program office
rows.period: Current reporting year plus the two prior annual submissions
rows.account: EMALS/AAG procurement funding as reported in two MSARs
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label 'EMALS subprogram' is being read as a self-contained launch-and-recovery scope, when the governing contract and reporting construct bundle EMALS with AAG across CVN-79 and CVN-80; the double-count risk therefore sits in the EMALS/AAG boundary, not in the EMALS/CVN-78 boundary. This label arrived with the question as posed.

rows.instruction: Obtain from PMS 378 the appropriation-to-expenditure crosswalk supporting the CVN-78 subprogram acquisition-funding display, including the line-level treatment of procurement line 2001 and every line flagged Shared or Sunk, and trace whether EMALS end-item funding appears once or twice across the CVN-78 and EMALS subprogram displays under the same appropriation.
rows.target_system: Navy budget/appropriation crosswalk supporting the MSAR funding display
rows.target_office: PMS 378 business financial manager
rows.period: Prior-years through current FYDP
rows.account: Procurement appropriation funding lines, incl. line 2001 and Shared/Sunk-flagged lines
rows.hypothesis: No authoritative inclusion statement exists in the MSAR at all, and the relationship is only derivable from the underlying appropriation-and-expenditure crosswalk — in which case the closing document is a funding-line reconciliation, not a narrative passage.

rows.instruction: Request the DCARC CSDR compliance assessment narratives behind both the CVN-78 subprogram Red rating and the EMALS Green rating, plus the CSDR plan WBS for each, and check whether launch-and-recovery WBS elements are reported in one plan, both, or neither. Also record the dollar-basis heading (then-year, base-year 2000, report-fiscal-year) on each estimate before any comparison is attempted.
rows.target_system: Defense Cost and Resource Center (DCARC) CSDR submission and compliance records
rows.target_office: DCARC; PMS 378; EMALS program office
rows.period: Current reporting year
rows.account: CSDR plans and compliance assessments; dollar-basis headings on acquisition estimates
rows.hypothesis: Any inclusion determination is unverifiable at the needed fidelity because the CVN-78 subprogram's cost-data reporting compliance is rated Red while EMALS-side reporting is rated Green; the asymmetry means the supporting cost-data pull cannot adjudicate overlap even if a narrative statement is found.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can the Navy Component Cost Estimate and the referenced OPNAV maintenance notices be obtained to trace the per-ship operating and support assumptions, including ship count, service life and inactivation treatment, down to a single hull?
rows.target_document: NCCA (Naval Center for Cost Analysis) and OPNAV N43/N98 maintenance notice holders
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Query NCCA's cost-estimate repository (Naval Center for Cost Analysis, OPNAV/ASN(RDA) cost-estimate library) for the CVN-78 class Component Cost Estimate supporting the MSAR O&S cost-element estimate; request the document control record only (title, date, approving official, classification/distribution caveat, CY2000 base-year statement) before requesting content. Period: the NCCE edition cited by the MSAR O&S section through the PB 2027 MSAR.
rows.target_document: Navy Component Cost Estimate, CVN-78 class (NCCA)
rows.target_office: NCCA
rows.account: O&S cost-element estimate, CVN-78 class
rows.hypothesis: The gap is a document-access problem, not an analytic one: the referenced Navy Component Cost Estimate (NCCE) for the CVN-78 class exists as a discrete NCCA deliverable with a date, signature authority and distribution list, and the per-ship O&S assumptions (ship count, service life, inactivation treatment) are stated in its O&S cost-element section. Closing the gap requires only an access determination, not new estimating work.

rows.instruction: Pull the MSAR O&S and disposal section source/estimate-origin footnotes for the CVN-78 subprogram and ask PEO Carriers/PMS 378 cost lead to identify the estimate of record and its approval authority; confirm whether any NCCE is cited as the source or only as a comparison. Period: current PB-cycle MSAR plus the preceding edition.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR, O&S and disposal sections
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers / PMS 378
rows.account: O&S and disposal estimate, CVN-78 class
rows.hypothesis: INHERITED LABEL: the attribution of the O&S estimate to a Navy Component Cost Estimate may be wrong — the reported current CVN-78-class O&S and disposal estimates are program-office estimates approved by the program manager, so the authoritative assumption set may sit with PMS 378/PEO Carriers rather than NCCA, and the "NCCE" label arrived with the question rather than from the document.

rows.instruction: Request from NCCA/PMS 378 a written statement of whether the O&S estimate is maintained at any level below the class average-annual-cost construct, and inspect the MSAR acquisition/O&S presentation to confirm the quantity basis is the multi-carrier class rather than CVN-79. Period: current MSAR edition.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR, O&S cost-element and quantity-basis sections
rows.target_office: NCCA / PMS 378
rows.account: O&S average annual cost per ship / ship count / service life
rows.hypothesis: The per-hull derivation fails not for want of documents but because the O&S total is constructed at class level from average annual cost per ship times ship count times service life; no CVN-79-specific per-hull O&S figure exists to be retrieved, and the inactivation-before-decommissioning treatment is a class service-life convention. The gap would then be closed by documenting non-existence rather than by obtaining a file.

rows.instruction: Ask OPNAV N43 (fleet maintenance) and N98 (air warfare) records custodians to identify, by serial and date, the maintenance notices cited in the CVN-78 Class MSAR O&S assumptions, and whether each is current or superseded; request the service-life and inactivation-scheduling paragraphs only. Period: from the notice dates cited in the MSAR to present.
rows.target_document: OPNAV N43/N98 maintenance notices cited in the MSAR
rows.target_office: OPNAV N43 / N98
rows.account: Service life and inactivation assumptions
rows.hypothesis: The OPNAV maintenance notices are the binding assumption source for service life and inactivation treatment, and they are held as serialized OPNAV N43/N98 correspondence with their own release authority — the citation in the MSAR may be to a superseded notice, so the obtainability question turns on identifying the current serial.

rows.instruction: Inspect the CVN-78 Class MSAR inactivation-and-disposal section and the EMALS subprogram entries for any stated allocation basis between the class total and individual hulls or subsystems; if none, obtain the NCCA disposal worksheet structure from the cost-estimate library. Period: current MSAR edition.
rows.target_document: CVN-78 Class MSAR, inactivation and disposal section
rows.target_office: NCCA / PMS 378
rows.account: Inactivation and disposal, carrier class including EMALS
rows.hypothesis: Even if the documents are obtained, a per-hull reconciliation will not close because the inactivation and disposal scope is carried at class level and bundles subsystem inactivation (including EMALS) into the carrier-class inactivation and disposal cost, so the inactivation element cannot be apportioned to CVN-79 without a stated split.

rows.instruction: Obtain from ASN(FM&B) FMB-6 the inflation rates-and-factors tables for the years spanning the O&S base year to the current report fiscal year, and extract the MSAR table headings that declare each column's dollar basis. Period: O&S base year through current PB cycle.
rows.target_document: ASN FMB-6 inflation rates and factors; MSAR table headings
rows.target_office: ASN(FM&B) FMB-6
rows.account: Dollar-basis conversion for O&S cost-element estimate
rows.hypothesis: Any per-hull O&S figure derived from these documents will be non-comparable to the acquisition presentation unless the dollar basis is pinned first: the O&S estimate is expressed in a stated base year with conversion sourced to ASN FMB-6 rates and factors, while the acquisition tables mix base-year, then-year and report-fiscal-year bases.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: For the CVN-79 contracts administered by DCMA, what estimate-at-completion and cost-to-complete documentation exists (Program Support Team collaboration site EACs, contractor-provided EAC/ETC methods and periodic updates, and the semiannual ACO reports to the PCO and program integrator), and can it be obtained?
rows.target_document: DCMA contract management office / Program Support Team for the shipbuilder, via the responsible ACO
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Ask the DCMA CMO responsible for the Newport News shipbuilder (via the named responsible ACO) for the current PST assignment roster / DCMA program integrator assignment memorandum covering the CVN-79 construction contract and its CLIN structure, for the period from contract award to the current fiscal year, and for the single question of whether a PST is assigned and whether the collaboration-site EAC is the ACO's EAC of record for those contracts. One roster lookup kills or confirms the premise.
rows.target_document: DCMA CMO PST / program-integrator assignment roster and designation memorandum for the CVN-79 construction contract
rows.target_office: DCMA contract management office supporting the shipbuilder — responsible ACO
rows.period: award of CVN-79 detail design and construction contract through current fiscal year
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79 full ship construction / detail design and construction contract line items
rows.hypothesis: The predicate label in the question — that a Program Support Team (PST) exists for the CVN-79 shipbuilder contracts and maintains an EAC on a collaboration site — is an inherited attribution rather than a verified fact; if no PST is assigned to these contracts, the PST-collaboration-site EAC artifact does not exist and the ACO instead holds only risk-based contractor EAC requests, which changes the entire document inventory sought.

rows.instruction: Request from the responsible ACO the contract's payment and financing clause list (Section I) and financing designation for the CVN-79 construction contract, and the ACO's statement of whether semiannual progress-payment/EAC reports to the PCO and program integrator were generated, for the two most recent semiannual reporting cycles. A clause-list page settles it without any contractor engagement.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract Section I payment/financing clauses and the ACO's semiannual progress-payment and EAC report transmittals to the PCO and program integrator
rows.target_office: DCMA responsible ACO; NAVSEA PCO of record
rows.period: two most recent semiannual reporting cycles
rows.account: CVN-79 construction contract financing line items
rows.hypothesis: The semiannual ACO report to the PCO and DCMA program integrator may not exist as a discrete retrievable document for these contracts because the reporting trigger is ACAT I/II progress-payment status; if the CVN-79 contracts are not progress-payment financed (or the financing clause differs), no semiannual EAC/progress-payment report was ever generated, and the gap is a non-existence finding rather than an access problem.

rows.instruction: Request from the responsible ACO the contract file index and the specific pre-approval document package for the initial progress/financing payment request on the CVN-79 construction contract — specifically the contractor's written CTC estimating methodology submission and the ACO's approval memorandum — for the period surrounding initial financing-request approval, under the records-management authority cited in the DCMA manual.
rows.target_document: Contract file index plus contractor written cost-to-complete estimating methods submission and ACO initial-request approval memorandum
rows.target_office: DCMA responsible ACO, official contract file
rows.period: initial financing payment request approval date through present
rows.account: CVN-79 detail design and construction contract
rows.hypothesis: The contractor's written methods for estimating cost to complete and for identifying costs of delivered, invoiced and accepted items — a one-time pre-approval artifact — exists in the official contract file and is retrievable as a file document, independent of any proprietary EAC data, so the cheapest closure path is the contract file index rather than a contractor data request.

rows.instruction: Ask the responsible ACO for the transmittal log or receipt record of contractor ETC updates for the CVN-79 contract for the last four semiannual cycles — dates received and proprietary markings only, not the substance — and ask the NAVSEA PCO whether written concurrence for third-party release of the marked ETC submissions can be granted. A transmittal log distinguishes 'does not exist' from 'exists but restricted' at near-zero cost.
rows.target_document: ACO receipt/transmittal log for contractor ETC updates and contractor proprietary markings sheet
rows.target_office: DCMA responsible ACO; NAVSEA PCO
rows.period: last four semiannual ETC update cycles
rows.account: CVN-79 construction contract
rows.hypothesis: The periodic (at-least-semiannual) contractor estimate-to-complete updates exist but are withheld as contractor proprietary/competition-sensitive data rather than absent, meaning the closability barrier is a release-authority question (contractor markings and PCO release concurrence), not a records question.

rows.instruction: Request from the responsible ACO the basic progress-payment review working papers and review conclusions filed in the CVN-79 contract file for the most recent two review cycles, limited to the physical-progress / work-in-process and liquidation-capability test sections, under the manual's contract-file currency and records-retention provisions.
rows.target_document: ACO basic progress-payment review working papers and conclusions for the CVN-79 contract
rows.target_office: DCMA responsible ACO
rows.period: two most recent progress-payment review cycles
rows.account: CVN-79 construction contract progress-payment line items
rows.hypothesis: Reported-cost-to-physical-progress reconciliation sought by the question is in fact documented in the basic progress-payment review working papers (tests of expended costs against physical progress, work-in-process value and liquidation capacity), so the blocking condition may be satisfiable from ACO review documentation even if contractor EAC/ETC files remain unavailable.

rows.instruction: Request from the DCMA CMO the ACO's temporary-withhold tracking record for the CVN-79 contract (cumulative by contract, per the manual's tracking requirement) and the corresponding MOCAS line-item withhold-line and WAWF current/cumulative withhold entries, by CLIN, for the current and prior fiscal year — identifying authority, effective date and affected CLIN only, no amounts needed to establish existence.
rows.target_document: ACO temporary-withhold tracking record; MOCAS line-item withhold lines; WAWF withhold entries for the CVN-79 contract
rows.target_office: DCMA responsible ACO; DFAS Columbus
rows.period: current and prior fiscal year
rows.account: CVN-79 construction contract CLINs/SLINs subject to withholds
rows.hypothesis: Part of the unexplained hull cost may not be an estimating-documentation question at all but an acceptance/withhold artifact — amounts invoiced net of withholds, missing-component withholds, or temporary technical-data withholds recorded at line-item level — which would show reported costs diverging from EAC-based projections for payment-mechanics reasons traceable in MOCAS/WAWF rather than in EAC files.

rows.instruction: query: For CVN-79 performance-based-payment or financing activity, can the ACO-approved payment amounts and the payment office's actual disbursed amounts be obtained and compared, and were any differences pursued and resolved?
rows.target_system: Responsible DCMA ACO and DFAS Columbus contract pay
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Request from the DCMA CMO administering the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract the contract file section holding PBP/financing approval and reconciliation documentation, naming the ACO of record, for the full period of PBP activity on the hull; ask specifically for any record of the required comparison of payment-office actual PBP amounts against ACO-approved amounts and any difference-pursuit correspondence.
rows.target_document: DCMA ACO contract file (PBP approval and reconciliation folder) for the CVN-79 contract
rows.target_office: Responsible DCMA CMO / warranted ACO for the CVN-79 contract
rows.period: full span of PBP activity on the CVN-79 contract
rows.account: CVN-79 performance-based payment / contract financing
rows.hypothesis: The comparison is already performed and documented as a routine ACO reconciliation step, so the artifact exists in the CVN-79 contract file and the gap is a retrieval problem, not a data-existence problem. Killing this is cheapest because a single contract-file request either produces the comparison record or proves it was never made.

rows.instruction: Pull from WAWF within PIEE all PBP/financing payment-request records against the CVN-79 contract number, including ACO approval actions and the ACO-completed ACRN worksheets used as special payment instructions, for the full PBP period; confirm whether approved amount and charged ACRNs are retrievable per request.
rows.target_document: WAWF PBP payment requests and ACO-completed ACRN worksheets
rows.target_office: PIEE/WAWF system owner; DCMA ACO as approver of record
rows.period: full span of PBP activity on the CVN-79 contract
rows.account: CVN-79 PBP requests and ACO approvals, by ACRN
rows.hypothesis: The ACO-approved amounts are recoverable in structured form from WAWF/PIEE, where the ACO's approval action records the amount and the ACRN worksheet records the accounts to charge; one system pull establishes whether the approved-side of the comparison is obtainable at all.

rows.instruction: Request from DFAS Columbus contract pay the MOCAS disbursement history for the CVN-79 contract number, limited to PBP/financing payment types, broken out by ACRN and payment-request identifier, for the full PBP period; ask whether approved-versus-disbursed variance reporting is produced for this contract.
rows.target_document: MOCAS contract disbursement history / payment ledger for the CVN-79 contract
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus contract pay
rows.period: full span of PBP activity on the CVN-79 contract
rows.account: CVN-79 PBP disbursements by ACRN
rows.hypothesis: The disbursed-side amounts are recoverable from the entitlement/disbursement record held by the named payment office, so the comparison is mechanically closable; this is killed or confirmed by one query to DFAS Columbus contract pay for the contract's disbursement history by ACRN.

rows.instruction: Request from the CVN-79 ACO the temporary-withhold tracking record and the WAWF entries showing current and cumulative withholds applied to approved PBP requests on the CVN-79 contract, including the contractual authority, effective date and any required DFAS action for each withhold, for the full PBP period.
rows.target_document: ACO temporary-withhold tracking record and WAWF withhold entries
rows.target_office: Responsible DCMA ACO for the CVN-79 contract
rows.period: full span of PBP activity on the CVN-79 contract
rows.account: CVN-79 PBP approved-request reductions and cumulative withholds
rows.hypothesis: Apparent approved-versus-disbursed differences are not errors but recorded reductions and withholds the ACO applied to the approved PBP requests, with current and cumulative amounts captured in WAWF; checking the withhold records explains the differences without any reconciliation failure.

rows.instruction: Read the payment-office block and financing clauses of the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract and its modifications to establish the designated payment office of record for PBP/financing; if it is not DFAS Columbus, request the ACO's documented direct confirmation of fund availability against the charged ACRNs from that office for the full PBP period.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract payment-office designation and contract financing clauses, with modifications
rows.target_office: PCO of record for the CVN-79 contract; designated payment office named in the contract
rows.period: contract award through end of PBP activity
rows.account: CVN-79 financing payment-office designation and fund-availability documentation
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label naming DFAS Columbus as the disbursing office for this hull's financing may be wrong; if the disbursement office is other than DFAS, the ACO's fund-availability confirmation and the comparison trail sit in a different office's records, and querying DFAS Columbus would return nothing and be misread as a records gap. The label arrived attached to the question as the named executor and has not been tested.

rows.instruction: Read the CVN-79 contract's financing terms and any PCO-concurred modifications establishing or renegotiating those terms to identify the actual financing instrument and payment-type classification used; then re-query WAWF and the payment office under that classification for the full financing period.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract financing clauses and PCO-concurred financing modifications
rows.target_office: PCO of record for the CVN-79 contract, with DCMA ACO concurrence file
rows.period: contract award through end of financing activity
rows.account: CVN-79 contract financing terms and payment-type classification
rows.hypothesis: The activity labeled 'performance-based payment' on this hull may actually be progress payments or another financing type carried under a different payment classification, in which case the approved-versus-disbursed records are filed under a different payment type and the comparison appears absent only because it was sought under the wrong label. The PBP characterization arrived with the question rather than from the contract.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Do any contractor debt determinations or collection actions exist against the CVN-79 contracts (handled under DCMA's contractor-debt procedures rather than through the financing-request stream), and can the debt and demand-letter records be obtained?
rows.target_document: Responsible DCMA ACO; DFAS Columbus debt management
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Ask the responsible DCMA ACO (CVN-79 shipbuilding CMO, Newport News) for the contract-file index covering the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract(s) for the full period of performance to date, and specifically for the list of unilateral and bilateral modifications coded as downward price adjustments/credits to the applicable SCN appropriation. A nil return on debt entries plus the presence of credit modifications kills the debt hypothesis in one request against a file the ACO is already required to keep current.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract file modification register and contract-file index
rows.target_office: DCMA CMO ACO of record for the CVN-79 contracts
rows.period: Contract award through most recent closed month
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79 construction line; contract-file modification register
rows.hypothesis: No contractor debt determination or collection action exists against the CVN-79 contracts at all; the gap is empty because the recovery activity that occurred was handled as a voluntary refund or a downward contract-price modification rather than as a debt, so nothing exists in the debt stream to retrieve and the exposure is correctly recorded as nothing left unexplained.

rows.instruction: Request from the same ACO the cumulative temporary-withhold tracking record required to be maintained by contract, limited to the CVN-79 contracts, plus the corresponding MOCAS withhold-line extract by CLIN/SLIN from DFAS Columbus. The ACO's tracking obligation means a single pull either produces the withhold inventory or shows none exists; either outcome resolves the record class cheaply.
rows.target_document: ACO cumulative temporary-withhold tracking record and MOCAS withhold-line extract
rows.target_office: DCMA ACO; DFAS Columbus contract pay
rows.period: Contract award through most recent closed month
rows.account: CVN-79 contract CLIN/SLIN withhold lines in MOCAS
rows.hypothesis: Debt-like activity against CVN-79 exists but is recorded as temporary payment withholds (missing components, late or deficient technical data, not-separately-priced sublines) rather than as debt determinations; the records sought are withhold decision memoranda and MOCAS withhold lines, not demand letters, so the search is aimed at the wrong record class.

rows.instruction: Pull the CVN-79 contract's payment clauses from the award document (Section I) to establish the financing type, then pull the WAWF progress/performance-based payment request history for the CVN-79 contract number showing current and cumulative withhold fields. If the contract is financed by progress payments with populated cumulative withhold fields, the premise that recovery runs through contractor-debt procedures is disconfirmed without touching DFAS debt management.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract Section I payment clauses; WAWF payment-request history
rows.target_office: DCMA ACO of record
rows.period: Contract award through most recent closed month
rows.account: CVN-79 financing payment requests, cumulative withhold fields
rows.hypothesis: The inherited label in the question — that any such recovery is "handled under DCMA's contractor-debt procedures rather than through the financing-request stream" — is wrong for CVN-79, because the hull is financed by progress or performance-based payments, where recovery is executed as a reduction of the approved payment request recorded in WAWF, and financing requests are expressly outside the cash-management/debt path. The attribution arrived with the question rather than from a cited source.

rows.instruction: Query DFAS Columbus debt management for the contractor-debt case inventory keyed to the CVN-79 contract numbers and to the prime contractor's CAGE, for the period from first payment to the most recent closed month, requesting demand-letter copies and cause codes distinguishing administrative-error debts from ACO-determined debts. Run this in parallel with the ACO file request so a nil at one office is not read as a program-wide nil.
rows.target_document: DFAS contractor-debt case inventory and demand letters
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus debt management
rows.period: First payment through most recent closed month
rows.account: Contractor-debt case file, CVN-79 contract numbers
rows.hypothesis: A debt exists but the demand letter is held by DFAS rather than the ACO, because the cause was a DFAS administrative payment error rather than a contract-interpretation dispute; searching only the ACO's contract file will produce a false nil return.

rows.instruction: Request from the DCMA CMO the QLOP analyses and resulting overpayment-recovery actions for the prime contractor for the period of CVN-79 performance, then cross-walk each action to contract number and CLIN to determine which attach to the CVN-79 hull. Cite the manual's records-maintenance requirement if the CMO asserts the analyses were not retained.
rows.target_document: QLOP analyses and overpayment-recovery correspondence
rows.target_office: DCMA CMO contract administration, prime contractor's cognizant office
rows.period: CVN-79 period of performance to date
rows.account: QLOP-derived overpayment actions, prime contractor CAGE
rows.hypothesis: Recovery activity originated from DCMA's analysis of quarterly limitation-of-payments or overpayment reports (QLOPs) and so exists as an overpayment-recovery action keyed to the contractor rather than indexed by hull; it will not surface under a CVN-79 search string and must be retrieved by contractor and contract number.

rows.instruction: Request from DFAS Columbus the history of withhold-line removals (not current balances) for the CVN-79 contract CLINs, and from the ACO the unilateral modifications discontinuing withholds plus the matching release invoices identifying the original shipment and CLIN. Also request the DCAA notifications issued on discontinuance, which provide an independent copy if the DCMA file is incomplete.
rows.target_document: MOCAS withhold-removal history; discontinuance modifications; release invoices; DCAA notifications
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus; DCMA ACO; cognizant DCAA field audit office
rows.period: Contract award through most recent closed month
rows.account: CVN-79 CLIN withhold-line removal history; deobligation modifications
rows.hypothesis: Records exist but are not obtainable at the requested granularity because the debt and withhold records were released or discontinued, with the MOCAS codes removed and the obligation adjusted by modification, leaving only a residual audit trail in the release invoice and the deobligation modification rather than a standing debt record.

rows.instruction: enumerate from inside the environment: What records retention and storage rules govern the CVN-79 payment records being requested (per the cited DCMA records-management volumes and the DCMA Records File Plan), and do they establish that the records for the hull's award years are still retrievable?
rows.target_system: DCMA records management / agency records officer
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Pull the records-maintenance paragraph and the reference/authority list of the DCMA payment-processing manual edition in force at CVN-79 award, and compare the authorities it actually cites against the volumes named in the gap statement; identify which source (question author, prior analyst memo, or the manual) asserted the volume citation.
rows.target_document: DCMA payment-processing manual, records-maintenance and references sections
rows.target_office: DCMA records management / agency records officer
rows.period: manual edition in force at CVN-79 award through present
rows.account: CVN-79 payment records retention authority
rows.hypothesis: The "cited DCMA records-management volumes" label arrived with the question and may not be the controlling authority for CVN-79 payment records; the manual's own retention clause may point to a different instruction/volume series or to the NARA-approved schedule rather than the volumes named in the gap text. The label should be tested before any retention conclusion is drawn.

rows.instruction: Request from the DCMA agency records officer the Records File Plan entries for contract administration/contract payment file series, with disposition authority and retention trigger as recorded for the fiscal years of CVN-79 contract award and option years.
rows.target_document: DCMA Records File Plan, contract payment and contract file series entries
rows.target_office: DCMA agency records officer
rows.period: CVN-79 award fiscal years
rows.account: contract administration / payment file series
rows.hypothesis: The question is closable off a single artifact: the DCMA Records File Plan line item covering contract-payment/contract-file records states its disposition authority and retention trigger, which either covers the hull's award years or shows the series cut off. One lookup resolves retrievability.

rows.instruction: Obtain from the cognizant DCMA CMO the contract file status (open / physically complete / closed) and closeout date for the CVN-79 contract and its modifications, and read it against the retention trigger wording in the applicable File Plan line.
rows.target_document: DCMA contract file closeout record / contract completion statement
rows.target_office: cognizant DCMA CMO contracts office
rows.period: award through current
rows.account: CVN-79 contract file closeout status
rows.hypothesis: Retention may run from a cutoff event (contract closeout or final payment) rather than from document creation, so an open or not-yet-closed CVN-79 contract would mean the retention clock has not started and the records remain retrievable regardless of award year age.

rows.instruction: Query DFAS Columbus MOCAS and the PIEE/WAWF program office for the retention/archive schedule and earliest retrievable transaction date for the CVN-79 contract number, covering invoices and receiving reports for the award years.
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus contract pay; PIEE program office
rows.period: award years to present
rows.account: MOCAS and WAWF payment and receiving-report transactions for the CVN-79 contract
rows.hypothesis: Even if the paper/official contract file series has aged out, the payment transaction records persist in the systems of record (MOCAS and WAWF/PIEE), which carry their own system retention rules distinct from the File Plan, so retrievability survives through system queries.

rows.instruction: Ask the cognizant CMO for retained annotated weekly MOCAS source-acceptance reports, temporary-withhold decision memoranda with authority and effective dates, and QLOP assessments filed in the official contract file system for the CVN-79 contract in the award fiscal years.
rows.target_document: annotated weekly MOCAS reports; withhold decision memoranda; QLOP assessments
rows.target_office: cognizant DCMA CMO / ACO of record
rows.period: CVN-79 award fiscal years
rows.account: audit-support payment documentation and withhold records
rows.hypothesis: Audit-support retention requirements attached to specific payment artifacts (annotated weekly MOCAS reports, withhold decision documentation, QLOP assessments) create a parallel retention obligation that may preserve reconcilable payment evidence for the award years even where the general file series has expired.

rows.instruction: Determine from the CVN-79 contract payment and acceptance clauses whether acceptance was source or destination and which CLINs were 2-in-1, then request the corresponding retention schedule and holdings from DFAS Columbus or the contract-designated approver office rather than DCMA.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract acceptance/payment clauses; DFAS records retention schedule
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus; contract-designated invoice approver
rows.period: CVN-79 award years
rows.account: destination-acceptance and 2-in-1 invoice records by CLIN
rows.hypothesis: The records being requested may not be DCMA-held at all for the relevant lines: destination-acceptance documentation is obtained and entered by DFAS Columbus, and 2-in-1 service invoices have no receiving report, so the governing retention rules would be DFAS schedules or the contract-designated approver's files, not the DCMA File Plan the question cites.

rows.instruction: enumerate from inside the environment: Can the MOCAS User Guide and the payment and receiving-report clauses incorporated in the CVN-79 contracts be obtained, to establish the meaning and completeness of the MOCAS data fields used in the reconciliation?
rows.target_system: DFAS Columbus MOCAS system documentation office; contract file holder
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Submit a documentation request to the DFAS Columbus MOCAS system documentation office named as executor, asking only two things: (1) the current MOCAS User Guide version number, issue date and distribution-restriction marking, and (2) whether a data dictionary of screen/field definitions is a separate deliverable from the User Guide. Do not request data. A one-page response either produces the control number or states no such consolidated guide exists, which kills or confirms this hypothesis in a single exchange.
rows.target_document: MOCAS User Guide and any associated MOCAS data dictionary
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus MOCAS system documentation office
rows.period: Current version in force at the date of the reconciliation extract
rows.account: MOCAS system documentation, obligation and disbursement field definitions
rows.hypothesis: The MOCAS User Guide is held and releasable by the named DFAS Columbus system documentation office as a single controlled document, and the gap is purely an access-authorization step rather than a missing artifact; the field-level definitions needed to map extracts to obligation and disbursement categories are already documented there.

rows.instruction: Identify which source asserted the title "MOCAS User Guide" in the gap statement (the dossier's own citation trail for PQ-a8652d97). Then ask the DFAS Columbus documentation office and the DCMA CMO jointly whether field definitions for the MOCAS Provisions screen and the following special-payment-instruction screen are published in the User Guide or in the DCMA manual. Cheap: the answer is a pointer, not a data pull.
rows.target_document: Gap PQ-a8652d97 source citation; DCMA contract administration manual; MOCAS Provisions screen documentation
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus MOCAS documentation office and administering DCMA CMO
rows.period: Version in force during CVN-79 contract administration
rows.account: Field definitions for MOCAS Provisions and special payment instruction indicator
rows.hypothesis: The label "MOCAS User Guide" arrived with the question and names the wrong artifact: the field-level meanings sought are carried in the DCMA contract administration manual provisions and the MOCAS Provisions/special-payment-instruction screens, not in a user guide. The gap is mis-addressed, so the request as written cannot be filled by any holder.

rows.instruction: Request from the CVN-79 contract file holder (PCO office of record, with the cognizant ACO copied) only the Section I clause index and the incorporated payment, receiving-report and electronic-submission clauses with their dates and any alternates, for the CVN-79 detail design and construction contract and its modifications. A clause index is routinely releasable and settles obtainability immediately.
rows.target_document: CVN-79 contract Section I clause list and incorporated payment/receiving-report clauses
rows.target_system: Electronic Document Access / contract file of record
rows.target_office: CVN-79 contract file holder (PCO of record) and cognizant ACO
rows.period: Contract award through the reconciliation cut-off, including all modifications
rows.account: Incorporated payment clauses and receiving report / DD Form 250 clauses
rows.hypothesis: The payment and receiving-report clauses are obtainable from the CVN-79 contract file at Section I rather than from any MOCAS source, and the contract file holder can produce the clause list without a full file release, so clause retrieval and guide retrieval are separable tasks with different closure paths.

rows.instruction: Request from the administering DCMA CMO the blank report formats and legends (not populated data) for the daily failed-receiving-report report, the weekly report of invoices awaiting source acceptance, and the report of invoices held for ACO approval, together with the retention citation for the annotated weekly copies. Blank formats with legends are low-sensitivity and either contain field definitions or demonstrably do not.
rows.target_document: Blank formats and legends for the cited recurring MOCAS reports; records retention citation
rows.target_office: DCMA CMO administering CVN-79; DFAS Columbus Contract Pay
rows.period: Reporting cycles covering the reconciliation window
rows.account: Receiving report, acceptance and held-invoice status fields
rows.hypothesis: Field-level meaning can be reconstructed operationally without the User Guide, because the named recurring MOCAS reports and their annotations already carry the mapping between receiving-report/acceptance status and payable obligation and disbursement categories; the reports' legends serve as the de facto data dictionary.

rows.instruction: Ask the cognizant ACO for the temporary-withhold tracking record required to be maintained by contract and across contracts, limited to CVN-79: for each withhold, the contractual authority, effective date, affected CLIN/supply line, MOCAS withholding code applied, and whether a request was made to DFAS Columbus to remove it from the line's withhold line. Existence or absence of this tracking record is a yes/no check.
rows.target_document: ACO temporary-withhold tracking record and associated unilateral modifications
rows.target_system: MOCAS withholding codes / Trusted Agent line-specific code requests
rows.target_office: Cognizant ACO, CVN-79; DFAS Columbus Contract Pay
rows.period: First withhold imposition through reconciliation cut-off
rows.account: Line-item withholds, withholding codes, and withhold-line entries
rows.hypothesis: The unexplained portion of the reconciliation is not a definitional problem at all but a withhold-accounting problem: amounts recorded at line-item level as missing-component or temporary withholds, and invoices billed net of withholds, are categorized in MOCAS in a way that will not reconcile to obligation and disbursement categories regardless of how the fields are defined.

rows.instruction: Ask DFAS Columbus to confirm, for the CVN-79 contract numbers, (1) whether any are ODO or otherwise paid outside the DCMA-administered default, and (2) which payment types on those contracts are excluded from cash management. In parallel ask the ACO for any PCO written concurrence on financing terms and any Contracts Director written concurrence for early release from cash management. A routing/coverage confirmation is far cheaper than a full extract reconciliation.
rows.target_document: DFAS payment-office routing confirmation; PCO and Contracts Director written concurrences; WAWF withhold records
rows.target_system: MOCAS, WAWF in PIEE, DCAA voucher processing
rows.target_office: DFAS Columbus Contract Pay; cognizant ACO and Contracts Director; DCAA cognizant office
rows.period: Award through reconciliation cut-off
rows.account: Contract financing, progress/performance-based payments, cost-voucher disbursements
rows.hypothesis: Some CVN-79 payment activity falls outside the DFAS-pays-DCMA-administered-contracts default or outside cash management (contract financing, public vouchers, progress or performance-based payments recorded in WAWF rather than MOCAS), so the MOCAS extract is structurally incomplete and no field definition will close the gap; the correct source is WAWF/PIEE and DCAA voucher records.

rows.instruction: retrieve and read: Can SUPSHIP produce the transaction-level supporting documentation for CVN-79 funding and payment actions, specifically the NAVCOMPT Form 2275 and ERP-generated Form 2276A work requests, the ERP approval histories and attachments for purchase requests, funding documents and project structures, and the written delegations of funds authority with the related certifying-officer payment documentation?
rows.target_document: SUPSHIP Newport News Comptroller (document request via NAVSEA FM)
rows.hypothesis: floor: the gap's own type and executor

rows.instruction: Ask SUPSHIP Newport News Comptroller, through NAVSEA FM, for a system-of-record crosswalk by fiscal year for the CVN-79 SCN line: a STARS-HCM/STARS-FL extract of open and closed CVN-79 obligation and disbursement records for FY10 and earlier plus FY11 shipbuilding-contract actions, against a Navy ERP extract of the same WBSE for FY11 forward. Confirm whether the pre-conversion population carries ERP approval histories at all.
rows.target_document: System-of-record crosswalk and dual extracts for the CVN-79 WBSE
rows.target_office: SUPSHIP Newport News Comptroller via NAVSEA FM
rows.period: FY10 through FY12, split at the ERP conversion boundary
rows.account: SCN, CVN-79 line
rows.hypothesis: The records exist but are split across two systems of record by fiscal year, so a single SUPSHIP ERP query cannot produce them: CVN-79 funding actions in FY10-and-earlier (and some early-FY11 shipbuilding-contract actions) live in STARS-HCM/STARS-FL rather than Navy ERP, which is why the ERP approval histories and attachments appear absent rather than missing.

rows.instruction: Trace the label back to its asserting source in the dossier (the financial-management manual passage distinguishing 2275 from 2276A), then ask PEO Aircraft Carriers / PMS 378 for the CVN-79 WBSE funding notifications to SUPSHIP Newport News stating authorized purpose and amount for the periods in question, and ask the SUPSHIP Comptroller whether any Economy Act Order document type was used for the same actions. If funding moved by WBSE allocation, the 2275/2276A request is void on its face.
rows.target_document: WBSE funding communications; NAVCOMPT Form 2275 / 2276A document-type inventory
rows.target_office: PEO Carriers / PMS 378 program office and SUPSHIP Newport News Comptroller
rows.period: Execution years covered by the reconciliation
rows.account: SCN CVN-79 WBSE
